title: Open PDF as an editable layout (reuse VectorCraft's PDF import)
author: mindmeltde
body:
**Use case**
Agencies regularly inherit print jobs where the client only has a PDF (old flyers, brochures, business cards; the original InDesign files are lost). Today DesignCraft can place a PDF as a graphic (crop boxes, page selection, layers), but not open it as an editable document. That makes DesignCraft a dead end for exactly the jobs where a free InDesign alternative would help most.

**Proposal**
File › Open on a `.pdf` (and `.ai` with PDF compatibility) builds a DesignCraft document:
- one page per PDF page, page size from the TrimBox/CropBox, bleed from the BleedBox
- vector art, images, colour (incl. spot colours and ICC-based spaces) as editable page items
- text as text frames with real characters and fonts
- best-effort reconstruction: lines → paragraphs, column detection → threaded frames, repeated items on every page → parent page, recurring font/size/leading combinations → paragraph/character styles

VectorCraft already reopens PDF and .ai editable (vectorcraft#79, #98: `crates/pdf/src/import*.rs` with text, shading, masks and colour import). Sharing that importer and adding the layout reconstruction on top seems the natural path.

**Out of scope / expectations**
Reconstruction is heuristic, like in Affinity or Scribus. A report (fonts substituted, items rasterised, frames that could not be threaded) after opening would be enough.

Happy to test with real-world agency PDFs (German text, CMYK, spot colours).

title: Placed CMYK TIFF images are exported as RGB
author: japbcoelho
body:
A CMYK TIFF placed in a document is written to the PDF as a DeviceRGB image, in PDF/X-4 exports too, so its ink values are lost: 100% K becomes RGB black and C0 M100 Y100 K0 becomes RGB red. A CMYK JPEG placed beside it keeps its CMYK data.

To reproduce on main `02f187c`, make a 200 × 100 px CMYK TIFF whose left half is 100% K and right half C0 M100 Y100 K0, and the same image as a JPEG, with Pillow:

```python
from PIL import Image
im = Image.new("CMYK", (200, 100), (0, 0, 0, 255))
im.paste((0, 255, 255, 0), (100, 0, 200, 100))
im.save("cmyk.tif", compression="tiff_lzw")
im.save("cmyk.jpg", quality=95)
```

Then place both and export PDF/X-4 with `designcraft-cli script -`:

```
file.new {}
selection.set {"ids": []}
file.place {"path": "cmyk.tif", "x": 72, "y": 72, "width": 200}
selection.set {"ids": []}
file.place {"path": "cmyk.jpg", "x": 72, "y": 250, "width": 200}
file.exportPdf {"path": "out-x4.pdf", "standard": "x4"}
```

In `out-x4.pdf` the TIFF is a `/DeviceRGB`, `/FlateDecode` image whose halves read (0, 0, 0) and (255, 0, 0). The JPEG is `/DeviceCMYK`, `/DCTDecode`, with the original (0, 0, 0, 255) and (0, 255, 255, 0). The export's `warnings` is empty: `check_pdfx4` doesn't look at colour spaces, so it misses DeviceRGB under the CMYK output intent (the page has no DefaultRGB either).

Expected: a CMYK raster keeps its CMYK values in the PDF, as a CMYK JPEG does. Failing that, the PDF/X-4 export should warn about the RGB image.

This matters most for K-only content such as text or line art in a TIFF. After the trip through RGB, conversion to the press profile turns it into four-colour black, which blurs when the plates are slightly out of register.

title: `designcraft-cli run`: --scale and --pdf-options are silently ignored when they appear after --export
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary
In `designcraft-cli run`, options given after `--export OUT` are accepted without any warning but have no effect. The same options given before `--export` work. The usage line (`run [--in FILE | --sample] [--cmd ...] [--page N] [--scale S] [--pdf-options JSON] [--export OUT] ...`) does not say that order matters.

## Environment
- Ubuntu (headless, no display), designcraft-cli 0.2.1 (linux x86_64 release tarball)

## Steps to reproduce
```sh
B=designcraft-cli
$B run --sample --export c.png --scale 0.5     # scale AFTER --export
$B run --sample --scale 0.5 --export d.png     # scale BEFORE --export
$B run --sample --export e.pdf --pdf-options '{"pages":"1"}'   # AFTER
$B run --sample --pdf-options '{"pages":"1"}' --export f.pdf   # BEFORE
```

## Expected
Both orders behave the same (or an error/warning is printed for an option that is ignored).

## Actual
```
wrote c.png (630×810, ...)     # --scale 0.5 ignored
wrote d.png (315×405, ...)     # --scale 0.5 applied
wrote e.pdf (4 pages, 552570 bytes)   # pages option ignored
wrote f.pdf (1 pages, 352342 bytes)   # pages option applied
```
Exit status is 0 in all cases and nothing is printed to stderr.

## Notes
- Measured n=2 per option (scale, pdf-options), repeated runs gave identical results.
- Not tested: other options placed after --export.

title: text.select / text.insert offsets (and get_story length) count UTF-8 bytes, not characters; this is not documented
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary
`get_story` reports `length: 15` for the 5-character story "はただ商店", and `text.select` anchor/focus values are interpreted as UTF-8 byte offsets. For non-ASCII text (e.g. Japanese) an agent that counts characters selects the wrong range. I could not find the unit stated in docs/mcp.md, docs/agents.md or the command's params description.

## Environment
- Ubuntu (headless), designcraft-cli 0.2.1, `designcraft-cli mcp` over stdio

## Steps to reproduce
In a fresh document (A4), via MCP `tools/call`:
1. `execute frame.create {"rect":[36,36,300,100],"content":"text","text":"はただ商店"}` -> story 9
2. `get_story {"story":9}` -> `"length": 15` (5 characters)
3. `execute text.select {"story":9,"anchor":0,"focus":1}` then `execute text.insert {"text":"Y"}`
4. `get_story {"story":9}`
Reset the text with `set_story_text` and repeat with focus 3 and focus 5.

## Expected
Offsets count characters (as the InDesign model does), or the unit is documented.

## Actual
| select 0..N | resulting text | length |
|---|---|---|
| 0..1 | `Yはただ商店` (nothing replaced) | 16 |
| 0..3 | `Yただ商店` (first character replaced) | 13 |
| 0..5 | `Yただ商店` (first character replaced; 0..5 spans 1.67 chars) | 13 |

So 3 units = 1 Japanese character, i.e. UTF-8 bytes. Offsets that fall inside a character are silently snapped.

## Notes
- n=3 (the table above), plus an earlier independent run with the same behaviour.
- Related but different: #61 (type_text after text.select).

title: MCP export_png / render_page accept a negative page index and silently export page 0
author: htdtkshi
body:

`page: -1` (and `-2`) is accepted by `export_png` and `render_page` and produces page 0, while `page: 5` on a 1-page document correctly returns `no page 5 (the document has 1 pages, indices are 0-based)`.

export_png {"page":-2,"path":"nm2.png"}
export_png {"page":4,"path":"n4.png"}

A negative index is rejected with the same kind of error as an out-of-range index (docs/mcp.md: "Page indices ... are 0-based").

title: [Feature Request] Import QuarkXPress (qxp, qxd) files
author: ewinnington
body:
QuarkXPress has two closely related native formats:

- .qxp — QuarkXPress Project: the modern native document format. It contains the actual page-layout project: pages/spreads, master pages, text boxes and linked text flows, image boxes and references, typography/styles, layers, colors, tables, guides, page geometry, etc. A .qxp can contain one or more layouts.

- .qxd — QuarkXPress Document: the older native QuarkXPress document format, primarily associated with QuarkXPress 3/4-era documents before Quark moved to the project-oriented .qxp format. There are still substantial archives of .qxd files from the 1990s and early 2000s.


For a new professional page-layout/design application, supporting them is strategically more important than their present-day market share might suggest.

The key is legacy corpus, not current Quark usage. QuarkXPress was one of the dominant professional DTP/page-layout systems before Adobe InDesign took over much of the market. Publishers, newspapers, agencies, corporate communications departments, printers and universities accumulated decades of Quark documents.

**InDesign doesn't provide a universal Quark archive importer.** 

-----
Why? My late father left me thousands of qxp / qxd files, including some which have a collection of his dreams, short stories, published manuscripts, letters to my family. Which are now in an unreadable / hard to access format. 

Allowing import of these is a hard reverse engineering problem, but unlocks millions of files across the world.

title: [Bug] Unrelated query values containing sample enable the sample magazine
author: Jagalite
body:
Unrelated URL parameter values containing `sample` enable the built-in sample magazine. For example, `?note=sample` and `?note=not_a_sample` behave like the documented `?sample` flag.

## Environment

- Current `main`: `d582277cc79c4bc9cee174b25b13fb11e6957aa5`, checked against the remote on 2026-10-07.
- Release browser build, Rust 1.95.0 and wasm-bindgen 0.2.129.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64; isolated headless Chrome 154.0.8037.93, Firefox 155.0 and Playwright WebKit 26.6 (not Safari).

## Reproduction

1. Open the browser app in a fresh profile with `?note=sample`.
2. Observe the initial document, then save it through File → Save.
3. Repeat with `?note=not_a_sample`.
4. Compare with the explicit flags `?sample` and `?webgl&sample`.

Expected: only an actual `sample` query flag enables sample startup. Unrelated parameter names and values should not activate it.

Actual: all four URLs open `Quarterly — Spring Issue`, with four pages and 25 items. Independent parsing of the actual downloaded native ZIPs confirms this in all three browsers. Reloading each URL produces the same sample again. Opening a separate one-page user document through the real chooser still works and saves correctly, so this is specifically startup flag parsing.

Both unrelated parameter variants reproduce once per browser, plus one reload per variant; the explicit sample flags are healthy controls. An initial user-document title comparison used its embedded title rather than the filename-derived title; that oracle was corrected against the retained saved outputs without rerunning the browser actions.

## Suspected cause and scope

`apps/designcraft-web/src/web.rs` checks `query().contains("sample")` rather than parsing query parameter names. The `webgl` flag uses a similar substring check, but this report confirms only the sample document behavior. This is a browser startup issue; no native application behavior or loss of unsaved user data is claimed.

title: RTL (Arabic): list bullets detach the first letter; multi-column frames and tables ignore right-to-left direction
author: EssaAlshammri

Arabic shaping, bidi and right-to-left paragraphs work well in general (including mixed Arabic/English and kashida justification). I found three places where layout doesn't follow the paragraph's right-to-left direction while setting an Arabic document:

### 1. Bullets in a right-to-left paragraph detach the first letter of each item

With `direction: rightToLeft` and `listType: bullets`, the first character of each paragraph is drawn next to the bullet, cut off from the rest of its word. That word loses its joining. For example, `بطاقة الهوية` renders as `•بـ    طاقة الهوية`.

**Expected:** the bullet on the right, followed by the whole word `بطاقة` intact. The same text without `listType: bullets` renders correctly (frame on the left in the repro).

**Expected:** for right-to-left text, the first column is the right one and text flows right → left.

Converting `١⇥٢⇥٣` (in a right-to-left paragraph) to a table puts cell `١` on the **left** and `٣` on the right.

**Expected:** for right-to-left text, the first column sits on the right. As it stands, Arabic tables have to be entered in reverse column order, which also flips the meaning of table-style `leftColumn` / `rightColumn`.

Hi! Thanks for the Crafting Apps. Having every app scriptable through MCP is a great base, and it made the following easy to build.

title: INDD import: bringing in indd-utils (clean-room INDD → IDML converter)
author: aiongg
body:
I've been working on a (nearly) feature complete clean-room INDD converter in a separate repo, [indd-utils](https://github.com/aiongg/indd-utils). We got a large number of publicly available INDD-IDML document pairs so that Claude could analyze them to build the format. It has quite a bit more than #98 (comparison below), so I'd like to figure out the best way to bring it into DesignCraft. It's still in progress, and since it's pretty large I'm not sure what the maintainers here would prefer. I've listed the options I see below, in order of my preference. Thoughts?

---

*The overview below was generated by Claude Opus 5.5.*

Related: #21 (INDD file support), #98 (another INDD importer).

## What it is

**indd-utils** (MIT OR Apache-2.0) is a Rust library and CLI (`indd`) that reads INDD and writes IDML. It's the same design as #98 (INDD → IDML in memory → DesignCraft's IDML importer), so DesignCraft's side stays small. It reads InDesign 3.0 to 2026 (21.x), little- and big-endian, has no dependencies and builds for wasm. Its output validates against InDesign's IDML RelaxNG schemas, except endnote markup, which it writes the way InDesign does and which the published schema rejects in InDesign's own files too. Public API: `indd::convert(bytes, name) -> { idml, warnings }`.

About 650 INDD files that come with an IDML exported by InDesign from the same document, and ~4,300 INDD files overall for robustness. The headline number is the share of InDesign's own IDML values that the converter reproduces exactly, counted on pairs where the IDML is known to match the INDD's last save. title: Issue 2: IDML table and cell styles are ignored (tables render with a 1 pt grid)
author: ludovic-coder
body:
What happens 
Tables imported from IDML that get their strokes from a table style and cell styles are drawn with a full black grid (outer border plus every vertical and horizontal cell edge). The styles are not applied.

IDML structure involved
- <Table AppliedTableStyle="TableStyle/Catalogue">
- The table style sets all border strokes to 0 and assigns region cell styles: HeaderRegionCellStyle="CellStyle/Header", BodyRegionCellStyle="CellStyle/Body row", LeftColumnRegionCellStyle="CellStyle/Pastille", with HeaderRegionSameAsBodyRegion="false" and LeftColumnRegionSameAsBodyRegion="false".
- The cell styles set left/right edges to weight 0 or Swatch/None, top edge weight 0, and a 0.5 pt black bottom edge.
- Most <Cell> elements only carry AppliedCellStyle="CellStyle/Body row" (or Header/Pastille) and no local stroke attributes; edge stroke priorities are present.

Expected 
Only a 0.5 pt rule under each row, no vertical rules and no outer border, as in the InDesign PDF.

Actual 
A default-weight grid on every cell edge plus an outer border. The header row and the left "Pastille" column also lose their own styling.

title: Windows startup crashes in AMD OpenGL driver; WGPU_BACKEND=dx12 launches successfully
author: DWAA1660
body:
## Problem
DesignCraft 0.4.0 on Windows opens briefly/spins and then crashes during startup. Reported on 8 October 2026.

Windows application crash records identify AMD OpenGL module `atio6axx.dll`, exception `0xc0000005` (invalid memory access). Launching the original executable reproduces the crash. Application files were present, the digital signature was valid, and Windows Installer records indicated successful installation configuration. The evidence identifies the crash location, but does not establish whether the underlying defect is solely in the driver or its interaction with DesignCraft.

## Reproduction and workaround
1. Launch the installed DesignCraft executable normally.
2. Observe the brief opening/spinner followed by process termination.
3. Launch with `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`.
4. DesignCraft opens and remains responsive.

The reporter verified a new DesignCraft window, a loaded DirectX 12 module, no loaded `atio6axx.dll`, and a successful startup log entry. Editing, saving, and exporting were not tested. GPU model, AMD driver version, and Windows build were not supplied.

## Separate shortcut problem
The first workaround shortcut failed because its PowerShell `-File` path pointed to normal application data while the launcher was saved in Codex's redirected application-data folder. Moving the launcher to Documents / DesignCraft Startup and correcting the shortcut fixed that separate path error. The launcher explicitly sets `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` and logs attempts to `Startup.log`.

## Expected behavior
The installed executable should select a safe Windows graphics backend before graphics initialization, without requiring a PowerShell launcher or custom desktop shortcut. An explicit backend override should remain available for troubleshooting.

## Scope
This is a startup workaround with successful reported verification, not a graphics-driver repair. Launching the original executable without the workaround may still crash.

title: [Bug] IDML import/export inverts layer order (backgrounds drawn over all content)
author: michaelperna
body:
**Summary**: IDML layers come in upside down. InDesign writes `<Layer>` elements in `designmap.xml` back to front, but the importer treats the first `<Layer>` as frontmost (`self.layers.push` in document order, and `Document::layers[0]` = front). Any InDesign file that puts a full-bleed background on its own layer renders as that background alone. The exporter writes layers front to back, so it has the same inversion going the other way.

**Evidence**
- I have a set of production signage templates, all exported from InDesign 21.6. Every `designmap.xml` lists the layers as `BLEED, Design Layout, Zone Digits, Cutcontour/drill holes, Guides`, the usual back-to-front stack with the die-cut and guides on top.
- InDesign's own PDF exports of those files draw the `BLEED` background behind everything.
- DesignCraft 0.4.0 (`designcraft-cli run --in x.idml --export x.pdf`) draws the background over everything, so every page comes out as one flat colour.
- Reversing the `<Layer>` elements in `designmap.xml` before import makes the DesignCraft render match InDesign's.

Worth confirming against InDesign 2026 with a two-layer document (create layers A and B, export IDML, check which comes first). Round-tripping DesignCraft → InDesign → DesignCraft would hide this, because both directions are inverted.

**Repro** (synthetic, generates `repro-layer-order.idml`: a red full-page rectangle on layer "Background", listed first, and the text FRONT on layer "Content", listed second)

title: [Bug] Text frames go overset when descenders don't fit; InDesign only requires the baseline to fit (+ CapHeight first baseline approximated)
author: michaelperna
body:
**Summary**: In InDesign, a line fits in a text frame when its **baseline** is inside the frame; descenders may hang below the bottom edge. `compose_with_db` requires `baseline + desc <= col.y1`. Tightly fitted InDesign frames (large display type, numbers in badges, two-line headings with explicit leading) therefore go overset on import and the text disappears.

A smaller related issue: `FirstBaseline::CapHeight` uses `asc * 0.72` rather than the font's cap height, which `Glyph::cap` already carries. `XHeight` uses `asc * 0.5` in the same way.

**Evidence**
- Production signage templates from InDesign 21.6 (Inter Bold, `FirstBaselineOffset="CapHeight"`, explicit leading): DesignCraft 0.4.0 preflight reports 21–54 overset frames per template, against 0 in InDesign.
- Example: 209 pt digits in a 186 pt-tall frame (vertical justification centre). The cap height (~152 pt) fits and the descender doesn't, so the frame comes out empty.
- Example: a two-line 185 pt heading with 190 pt leading in a 328.5 pt frame. Line 2's baseline is at ~324.5 pt (fits), with its descender at ~369 pt.
- With the patch below, overset frames drop from 54→15, 27→3, 25→12 and 21→15 on four templates. Most of what remains is line width (see the optical-kerning issue).

**Repro** (synthetic, generates `repro-line-fit.idml`. Put Inter (OFL) in a `Document Fonts` folder next to it)

```python
"""Synthetic IDML repros for two DesignCraft import/composition bugs. No third-party content."""
import zipfile
HDR='<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>\n'
PKG='xmlns:idPkg="http://ns.adobe.com/AdobeInDesign/idml/1.0/packaging"'
def designmap(layers, stories):
    L="".join(f'<Layer Self="{s}" Name="{n}" Visible="true" Locked="false" Printable="true"/>' for s,n in layers)
    S="".join(f'<idPkg:Story src="Stories/Story_{s}.xml"/>' for s in stories)
    return HDR+f'<?aid style="50" type="document" readerVersion="6.0" featureSet="257" product="21.0(1)" ?>\n<Document {PKG} DOMVersion="21.0" S…

title: [Feature] Optical kerning falls back to metrics, so InDesign-imported text sets wider
author: michaelperna
body:
**Summary**: `KerningMethod="$ID/Optical"` is imported as `Kerning::Optical`, but shaping treats it exactly like `Metrics` (`compose/src/shape.rs`: `if !matches!(p.kerning, Kerning::Metrics | Kerning::Optical)`). InDesign's optical kerning tightens pairs such as `Te`, `“P` and `k”` considerably in display type. Text set with Optical in InDesign is therefore wider in DesignCraft, and tightly fitted frames rewrap and go overset.

**Evidence**: in production signage templates, `Text “Park”` at 68 pt Inter Bold fits on one line of a 367 pt column in InDesign. DesignCraft breaks it after `Text` and pushes the rest of the story into overset. Applying tracking −40 to the same text in DesignCraft makes it fit. This is the main remaining difference after the layer-order and line-fit fixes (#179, #180).

Optical kerning is Adobe's own algorithm, so an exact match may not be possible. An approximation, or at least a preflight warning ("Optical kerning approximated by metrics"), would help imported documents.

title: Stacks records on top of each other when the document uses facing pages
author: brodyos-dev
body:
# `data.merge` stacks records on top of each other when the document uses facing pages

**Version:** DesignCraft 0.1.1, macOS universal DMG

## Summary
With `facingPages: true`, merged records after the first land at identical coordinates on the same page of one spread (overlapping), and a following page is left empty. With `facingPages: false` the same merge works correctly.

## Steps to reproduce (control channel, 127.0.0.1:7979)
1. `file.new` `{"pages":1,"width":612,"height":792}` (facing pages default on)
2. `frame.create` `{"spread":0,"rect":[72,72,540,200],"shape":"text","content":"text","text":"<<Title>> - <<Clue>>","caret":false}`
3. `data.merge` `{"rows":[{"Title":"Case 1","Clue":"Cellar"},{"Title":"Case 2","Clue":"Attic"},{"Title":"Case 3","Clue":"Garden"}],"spread":0}`
   Returns `{"pages":3,"records":3}`.
4. `document.inspect`

## Expected
Three records on three pages, each frame on its own page (p1 right, p2 left, p3 right of the following spread).

## Actual
- Spread 0: 1 frame (Case 1).
- Spread 1: **2 frames, both with bounds `[72,72,540,200]`**, so Case 2 and Case 3 overlap on the left page; the right page of spread 1 is empty.
- PDF export (3 pages): page 2 text extracts as "Case 32 - Garden / Attic" (overlapping); page 3 is blank.

Same steps with `facingPages:false` give 3 spreads with one frame each, correctly placed. CSV input works with the `csv` param as CSV text (a file path gives "no records", which is user error on my side).

## Impact
Merge cannot be used to generate pages in a facing-page (book) layout.

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to DesignCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

DesignCraft offers only manual interface themes. Window → Interface Color Theme lists "Dark", "Medium Dark" (the default), "Medium Light", "Light" and "High Contrast", defined by `Brightness` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` and persisted in `ui.json`. Restyling uses only the saved choice; no code path reads the OS appearance.

Because DesignCraft only has manual choices, a user whose macOS appearance switches automatically has to change the app theme by hand at least twice a day, or leave it mismatched with every other app.

## Proposed behavior

Add System to the existing theme choice. With System selected, the app applies a light theme while macOS is in Light mode and a dark theme while it is in Dark mode, both at launch and immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes. The existing manual choices keep working as they do today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The theme control offers a System choice (for example "System" or "Use system setting") alongside the existing manual choices, and every place that exposes the theme (Window → Interface Color Theme) shows it.
2. With System selected, the app starts in its light theme when macOS is set to Light and in its dark theme when macOS is set to Dark.
3. With System selected and the app running, changing the macOS appearance, including the scheduled change made by macOS Appearance "Auto", switches the whole interface (panels, menus, dialogs and custom-painted surfaces) to the matching theme without a rest…

title: mcp: add --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root so the server can be confined to a folder
author: MazenGit
body:
## Summary

`designcraft-cli mcp` has no way to confine file access to a folder, so an agent connected to it can read and write anywhere the user can. Please add root flags matching PhotoCraft's `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root`.

## Environment

- DesignCraft: `designcraft-cli 0.4.0` (v0.4.0, windows-x64 portable zip, checksum and signature verified)
- Windows 11 Home, 10.0.26200
- Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9549

## Command

```powershell
designcraft-cli.exe mcp --automation-read-root C:\Users\<user>\work --automation-write-root C:\Users\<user>\work
```

## Expected

The server starts and only reads from and writes under the given folder, as PhotoCraft's does.

## Actual

Exit code 1, nothing on stdout, and on stderr:

```text
designcraft-cli: unknown mcp option `--automation-read-root` (usage: designcraft-cli mcp [--connect PORT] [--sample])
```

The usage line shows the only supported options, so there is currently no sandbox option.

## Request

Add root flags to `mcp` that match PhotoCraft's (`--automation-read-root <dir>`, `--automation-write-root <dir>`), so one client config works across the suite. PhotoCraft's earlier work on this (photocraft#676, photocraft#1551) and PdfCraft's `--root` confinement (pdfcraft#136, pdfcraft#137) are prior art.

usage: designcraft-cli run [--in FILE | --sample] [--cmd ID[=JSON]]... [--page N] [--scale S] [--pdf-options JSON] [--export OUT] [--all-pages DIR]
       designcraft-cli commands [FILTER]
       designcraft-cli describe COMMAND
       designcraft-cli script [FILE|-] [--in FILE | --sample] [--connect PORT] [--save OUT] [--export OUT] [--keep-going]
       designcraft-cli app [--port PORT] COMMAND [JSON] | --method METHOD [JSON]

author: thaynej

### What happens
When a .docx has tracked changes that include a **move**, placing it in DesignCraft drops the moved text entirely. It disappears from the old spot, which is correct, and never shows up in the new spot.

      <w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">INSERTED</w:t></w:r>
    </w:ins>

title: Fonts activated by font services (Adobe Fonts) aren't found: port VectorCraft #579
author: thaynej
body:
### What happens
On a Mac where Adobe Fonts are active through Creative Cloud, DesignCraft reports them as missing. For example, an IDML set in Minion 3 and Acumin Pro opens with both fonts substituted, even though InDesign, Word and other apps on the same Mac use them.

### Why
`system_font_dirs()` in `crates/fonts/src/fontdb.rs` only scans font folders (on macOS: `/System/Library/Fonts`, `/Library/Fonts`, `~/Library/Fonts`, the MobileAsset font folders and Office's `DFonts`; on Windows: `Fonts` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts`). Font services such as Adobe Fonts don't install into those folders. They register their fonts with the operating system while they run, which is how other apps see them.

### Suggested fix
VectorCraft just solved this (storytold/vectorcraft#579): it asks the OS for its font list as well as scanning the folders. On Windows it uses DirectWrite's system font collection (5854346, aa5e8f4), and on macOS it uses CoreText's `CTFontManagerCopyAvailableFontURLs` (4b00c2d), reading the files in place. Doing the same in DesignCraft would fix it on both platforms without depending on where any service keeps its files.

This deliberately does **not** scan Creative Cloud's own storage folder. Adobe treats those files as private (an Adobe community manager: "extracting font files from their obscured location is a violation of Adobe's terms of service"), while using activated fonts in third-party desktop apps through the system is the supported route. `file.package` already leaves out fonts whose licence restricts copying, and that should keep covering these.

One design point is yours: VectorCraft's versions use a scoped `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` for the CoreText/DirectWrite calls, and DesignCraft currently forbids `unsafe`.

Related: #48 / #107 (installed fonts in general, fixed in 0.4.0).

In the interest of full disclosure, this was found and analysed with an AI assistant (Claude).

title: Autoflow adds dozens of empty pages when placed text starts with a page break
author: thaynej
body:
### What happens
Placing a .docx whose first paragraph holds only a page break (common in sections split out of a longer Word file) with `autoflow: true` adds far more pages than the text needs. Every page after the first one with text holds only an empty threaded frame.

### Steps to reproduce
A synthetic .docx: a paragraph with only `<w:r><w:br w:type="page"/></w:r>`, then three short paragraphs (`A Short Heading`, `First short paragraph of made-up text.`, `Second short paragraph of made-up text.`), 98 characters in all.

DesignCraft 0.4.0, new Letter document, `file.place {path, page: 1, autoflow: true}`:

| File | `pagesAdded` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| with the leading page break | **33** | page 1 blank (fine: the break asks for that), text on page 2, pages 3–34 hold empty threaded frames |
| same file without the break | 0 | everything on page 1 |

The count grows with the text: a real one-page section of 813 characters gave `pagesAdded: 271`.

**Expected:** 1 page added (page 1 blank, the text on page 2).

### Likely cause
`autoflow()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/place_text.rs` estimates how many frames it still needs from how much the existing frames show: `per_frame = shown.max(at) / frames`, then `want = (len - at).div_ceil(per_frame)`. A frame that ends at a page break shows almost nothing, so `per_frame` comes out at a few characters. Autoflow then adds roughly one page per few remaining characters in a single batch, and doesn't remove the frames it didn't need. The same overestimate would hit any frame cut short by a break, not only one at the start.

Possible fixes: base the estimate only on frames that ended because they were full, or add pages a few at a time, or drop trailing frames and pages that end up empty once the story fits. I'm happy to try a PR if you have a preferred approach. In the interest of full disclosure, this was found and analysed with an AI assistant (Claude).

title: Feature request: unified, stackable text styles (one kind of style, like CSS classes)

### The need I'm an art director and have used InDesign daily for more than ten years. Two limitations of its style model have bothered me the whole time. **One style per range.** If I want bold text, I create a "Bold" style. If I want italic text, I create an "Italic" style. If I want both, I have to create a third style, "Bold Italic", although the two I already have describe exactly what I want. Bold and italic are only the simplest case. The same is true of every typographic attribute: typeface, size, weight, width, all caps, tracking, colour, alignment, justification and so on. body:
InDesign writes some `AppliedFont` values with its `$ID/` prefix (for example `$ID/Arial` in IDML exported from InDesign 21.6 on Windows). DesignCraft looks the family up with the prefix still attached, so the font is reported missing even when it is installed or sits in `Document Fonts`.

**Repro** (designcraft-cli 0.5.0, main @ 92649ff)
1. Export any IDML from DesignCraft with a bundled font (Source Serif 4).
2. In the story XML change `<AppliedFont type="string">Source Serif 4</AppliedFont>` to the value in the table.
3. `file.openIdml {path}` then `font.list {}`.

| AppliedFont in the IDML | font.list |
|---|---|
| `Source Serif 4` | ok |
| `$ID/Source Serif 4` | **missing** |
| `Source Serif 4 (OTF)` | ok (fixed by #247) |
| `Nope Sans` | missing (control) |

Seen on a real job: a 2-page program exported from InDesign 21.6 (Windows) with Arial throughout opened with Arial missing until `$ID/` was stripped from the IDML; after that all 32 stories matched InDesign's text.

**Suggestion:** strip a leading `$ID/` when resolving `AppliedFont`, next to where #247 strips the format suffix.

title: file.package with idml: the IDML embeds images and links to the build machine's absolute paths, so it doesn't relink elsewhere
author: director-LAC
body:
The IDML that `file.package {idml: true}` writes embeds every image and points each link at an absolute path on the machine that built it. A package built on Linux and opened in InDesign on Windows therefore arrives with all images embedded rather than linked to the package's `Links/` folder.

**Repro** (designcraft-cli 0.5.0, main @ 92649ff)
```
file.new {"width": 612, "height": 792, "pages": 1}
frame.create {"rect": [36, 200, 300, 400], "content": "graphic"}
file.place {"path": "/abs/path/mascot.pdf", "frame": "$1.id", "pdfCrop": "media"}
file.package {"dir": "/abs/path/pkg", "idml": true}
```

| IDML | Size | Image bytes in spread XML | LinkResourceURI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file.exportIdml` (default) | 15,566 B | yes | `file:/abs/path/mascot.pdf` |
| `file.exportIdml {embedImages: false}` | 9,597 B | no | `file:/abs/path/mascot.pdf` |
| `file.package {idml: true}` | 15,572 B | **yes** | `file:/abs/path/pkg/Links/mascot.pdf` |

`embedImages: false` works on `file.exportIdml`, but the package uses the embedding default even though it has just copied every file into `Links/`.

**Measured in InDesign 21.6 (Windows), IDML built on Linux**
- All 11 placements on one page arrived `LINK_EMBEDDED`.
- A 20-page IDML grew from 0.38 MB (InDesign's) to 70.7 MB.
- Links resolved (36 of 36) only after we rewrote the URI prefix to the Windows `Links` folder.

title: Suggestion: say what you're working on before you start (draft PR or issue comment)
author: aiongg
body:
With many people contributing at once, the same work is getting done more than once. Today alone there were two fixes for #338, three for #201, two for the Type tool's click selection and overlapping CJK work, each written without knowing about the others.

A light convention would avoid most of it:

- Before starting, search open PRs and issues for the topic.
- When you start, comment on the issue ("working on this") or open a draft PR right away, even with nothing in it yet. Mark it ready for review when it's done.
- For work that has no issue yet, open one first, saying what you plan to change.

A short CONTRIBUTING.md (or a line in the README) stating this would make it the default. This is only a suggestion; how contributions are coordinated is up to the maintainers.

title: No Break override makes spaces fixed-width in justified text, so lines get letter-spaced
author: dmuhr
body:
**Version:** DesignCraft 0.5.0 (build 4e0e3949f1eb), macOS 15

**What happens**
Applying a No Break override (`noBreak: true`) to the full text of a line inside a justified paragraph makes the spaces in that run fixed-width. When the paragraph is justified, the extra space is spread as **letter spacing** across the glyphs instead of being added to the word spaces.

**Expected**
No Break should only stop line breaks inside the run. The spaces should still stretch and shrink for justification, as in InDesign, where a No Break run is justified with word spacing like any other text.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Text frame ~61 mm wide, paragraph `align: leftJustified`, 7.6 pt text, a paragraph long enough for several lines.
2. Apply `{"noBreak": true}` as a character override to the text of one full line (excluding its first and last character).
3. Render the page (`ui.render`) or export a PDF.

**Result**
The No Break line is justified with wide letter spacing; the other lines use normal word spacing. Very visible at body sizes.

No Break is the standard way to keep names, numbers and units together in justified text. Right now any No Break run that ends up on a justified line gets letter-spaced.

Provide a supported CLI invocation with DesignCraft desktop distributions on Windows, Linux, and macOS, so people, scripts, and agents can lay out a publication or export a page through a documented invocation.

Desktop acquisition does not imply a command is available in a shell. Windows packages include `designcraft-cli.exe` without adding it to PATH. Preserve native Linux commands and document Windows install paths and portable executables. Make the CLI accessible to AppImage and Flatpak users through supported invocations. For macOS, include the CLI with desktop acquisition or provide an integrated matching install route.

title: Perspective of editorial designer for developers. :)
author: marysia-b
body:
Hi, I’m writing from the perspective of a graphic designer.

Automated correction of typographic errors is one of InDesign’s most important features. It saves publishers and designers many hours of work, sometimes even days!!

If designers had to handle these issues manually, they would have to wait until the very end of the project before showing clients a polished, professionally typeset layout, simply because they’d be worried about further changes to the text. All it takes is for an author (of text) to add a single sentence, and the layout of dozens of pages can be thrown off, forcing the designer to make time-consuming adjustments throughout the book.

That’s why typographic automation is one of the most important features of InDesign, and one of the reasons Adobe has managed to retain hundreds of millions of users in its ecosystem for over 15 years. On the market there is no another program which is able to do that. Long time ago people used QuarkXPress... but it is really outdated program.

If DesignCraft doesn’t implement this feature properly in future, I honestly don’t think it stands a chance of convincing anyone to seriously consider abandoning Adobe in favor of the ArtCraft suite even if it will be as good, as Affinity is.

I’m familiar with many of Adobe’s applications, and almost every one of them has some great alternatives offered by competitors. We have got Blender, DaVinci, Corel, Affinity 3, Affinity Suite 2, Canva, CapCut, Framer, Figma... And many, many others! But InDesign is a key application! It’s fundamental. title: Cut, Duplicate, Paste in Place and pasting text leave an extra undo step that does nothing
author: noah1400
body:
**What happens**
Some commands record two undo steps for one action. The first Undo reverts the action, the second changes nothing, and only the third goes further back.

**Steps** (main a9124a0, headless with `designcraft-cli script`)
```
file.new {"pages": 1}
frame.create {"rect": [36, 36, 136, 136]}
selection.set {"ids": ["$1.id"]}
edit.cut {}
document.history {}
```
`document.history` answers `{"undo": ["Create Frame", "Clear", "Cut"]}`. `edit.undo` answers `Cut` and brings the frame back; a second `edit.undo` answers `Clear` and changes nothing.

The same happens with:
- `edit.duplicate`: `["Move", "Duplicate"]`
- `edit.pasteInPlace`: `["Paste", "Paste in Place"]`
- `edit.paste {"text": "…"}` at an insertion point: `["Type", "Paste"]`

**Expected**
One undo step per action, as `script.run` and tool gestures already give.

**Cause**
`Session::execute_unguarded` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`) records an undo entry for every undoable command, also when it runs inside another command (`edit.cut` runs `edit.clear`). `script.run` collapses its steps' entries by hand; other commands don't.

I'm working on this.

title: object.group panics when the objects are inside a group
author: noah1400
body:
**What happens**
`object.group` panics with "index out of bounds" when none of the named objects is a top-level object on the first object's spread, for example when both are already inside a group. The crash guard turns it into an error on desktop; the never-crash rule says a command must not panic.

**Steps** (main a9124a0, headless with `designcraft-cli script`)
```
file.new {"pages": 1}
frame.create {"rect": [36, 36, 136, 136]}
frame.create {"rect": [200, 36, 300, 136]}
object.group {"ids": ["$1.id", "$2.id"]}
object.group {"ids": ["$1.id", "$2.id"]}
```
The second `object.group` answers ``internal error in `object.group` (the document was kept as it was): index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0`` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs:1315`).

The same panic comes from:
- `selection.set {"ids": [...], "content": true}` on the two nested objects, then `object.group {}`
- `states.create {"ids": [...]}` with the nested ids (it runs `object.group`)
- a nested object first, plus an object on another spread

**Cause**
`group` collects the named objects that are top-level items of the first object's spread and then indexes the first of them. For nested objects that list is empty.

**Related, not a crash**
Grouping a nested object with a top-level one, or two objects on different spreads, makes a group of one and silently leaves the other out.

**Expected**
An error that says what can be grouped, and no panic.

title: GREP styles silently ignore invalid patterns (e.g. lookbehind)
author: noah1400
body:
## Problem

A GREP style with a pattern the regex engine can't compile is accepted without any error and then never applies. The user gets no feedback; the style just "doesn't work".

This hits people coming from InDesign: GREP styles there commonly use lookbehind, e.g. for Polish/Czech one-letter words (see #405):

    (?<=\s)[aiouwzAIOUWZ]\s

DesignCraft uses the `regex` crate, which doesn't support lookbehind. The paragraph style is created, the pattern is silently dropped in `crates/compose/src/overlay.rs` (`Regex::new(..).ok()`, and `None` is skipped).

Find/Change already handles this correctly: an invalid GREP there returns `bad GREP: …` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/find.rs`).

## Steps to reproduce

1. `style.character.create` with `{"name": "Sierotki", "chars": {"noBreak": true}}`
2. `style.paragraph.create` with `{"name": "PL", "para": {"grepStyles": [{"style": "Sierotki", "pattern": "(?<=\\s)[aiouwzAIOUWZ]\\s"}]}}`
3. Apply `PL` to a text frame with Polish text in a narrow column

**Expected:** an error saying the pattern is invalid (or the style works).
**Actual:** no error, and the GREP style has no effect. In a headless test at 35 column widths, lines ending with a one-letter word went from 124 of 343 to still 124 of 343. The equivalent pattern without lookbehind, `\b[aiouwzAIOUWZ]\s`, brings that down to 0.

## Proposed fix

- `style.paragraph.create` / `style.paragraph.edit` (and anything else that sets `grepStyles`) reject an invalid pattern with the regex error, as Find/Change does.
- The GREP Style section of Paragraph Style Options shows the error instead of saving the pattern.
- IDML import keeps the style but reports a warning, so one bad pattern doesn't stop a document from opening.

## Open questions

- **Lookbehind support** (e.g. via `fancy-regex`) would make more InDesign GREP styles work as-is. It's a separate decision: backtracking runs on every recompose, and patterns from imported files would need a backtrack limit.
- **Metacharacters:** Fi…

title: Bug: single-sided document: a page shows the last page of a two-page parent spread instead of the first
author: kenny-t-vo
body:
**DesignCraft 0.5.0** (macOS universal).

In a single-sided document (`FacingPages="false"`), a page that applies a two-page parent spread shows the parent's **second** page. InDesign 2026 shows the parent page in the same position as the document page, here the first. Documents built from templates with two-page parents lose their footers and running items.

**Repro.** `python3 make_idml.py` (below) writes `parent-pages.idml`: one Letter page applying parent A, whose first page holds "ITEM ON PARENT PAGE 1" and whose second page holds "ITEM ON PARENT PAGE 2".

```
designcraft-cli run --in parent-pages.idml --export out.pdf
pdftotext out.pdf -
```

| | Text on page 1 |
|---|---|
| InDesign 2026 (21.4): the IDML opened and exported to PDF | Page 1 applies parent A, a two-page parent spread. / **ITEM ON PARENT PAGE 1** |
| DesignCraft 0.5.0 | Page 1 applies parent A, a two-page parent spread. / **ITEM ON PARENT PAGE 2** |

Likely cause: `parent_page_for` in `crates/doc/src/build.rs` takes the parent's first page only for a left-hand page, and its last page otherwise, whatever the document's facing setting.

The script also writes `all-caps.idml`, which DesignCraft renders as InDesign does. Only its PDF text layer differs: DesignCraft keeps the typed case where InDesign's text extracts in capitals.

<details><summary>make_idml.py</summary>

```python
"""make_idml.py: writes parent-pages.idml and all-caps.idml, two small Letter documents for DesignCraft bug reports.

title: Bug: placed SVG: text never uses installed fonts (Arial, Georgia) and can fall back from sans to serif
author: kenny-t-vo
body:
**DesignCraft 0.5.0** (macOS universal).

A placed SVG's text is set in the bundled Source Sans 3 or Source Serif 4, even when the families it names are installed. A sans (Arial) can come out in a serif. InDesign 2026 sets the same SVG in the installed fonts. Text frames in the same documents do find Arial; only SVG text misses it.

**Repro.** Place `fonts.svg` (below) on a new Letter page:

```
designcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.new={"preset":"Letter"}' --cmd 'file.place={"path":"/abs/path/fonts.svg","x":36,"y":36}' --export out.pdf
pdffonts out.pdf
```

| Line | `font-family` | InDesign 2026 | DesignCraft 0.5.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Arial, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, sans-serif` | Arial | Source Sans 3 |
| 2 | `font-family: ArialMT, Arial` (in `style`) | Arial | Source Serif 4 |
| 3 | `Arial`, bold | Arial Bold | Source Serif 4 Bold |
| 4 | `Georgia` | Georgia | Source Serif 4 |
| 5 | `Source Serif 4` | Arial | Source Sans 3 |

Arial and Georgia are in `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental`. `select_font` in `crates/images/src/lib.rs` means to load installed families ("A family the SVG names that isn't bundled comes from the shared fonts (installed ones too)"), but they don't reach the text.

**Where it bites:** maps and diagrams exported as SVG from other tools (QGIS, matplotlib, scripts) and placed in a layout change typeface.

<details><summary>fonts.svg</summary>

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="160" viewBox="0 0 400 160">
<text x="10" y="30" font-size="20" font-family="Arial, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, sans-serif">1 Arial in a family list</text>

author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

`file.exportHtml` and `file.exportText` write real HTML, plain text and RTF. `designcraft-cli run --export` only special-cases `.pdf`, `.epub`, `.idml` and `.designcraft`. Every other extension, including `.html`, `.htm`, `.rtf` and `.txt`, is saved as a PNG of the first page and the process exits 0. The stderr line even reports pixel size and a glyph count. Docs list HTML as a `.html` export (`docs/file-format-parity.md`) and the engine command is `file.exportHtml`.

Not the same as #314 (HTML export content is basic). That command works; the CLI flag never calls it.

**Environment**

- DesignCraft v0.6.0 @ a9124a0517594ce9872f73637e7b841a4967bcf9, `designcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64, Rust 1.99.0

```sh
designcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'file.new={"pages":1}' \
  --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[72,72,400,200],"content":"text","text":"Hello HTML"}' \
  --cmd 'file.exportHtml={"path":"real.html"}' \
  --export via.html \
  --export via.rtf \
  --export via.txt
file via.html via.rtf via.txt real.html
```

**Expected**

`via.html` is the same kind of HTML document `file.exportHtml` writes (here, a file starting with `<!DOCTYPE html>` that contains `Hello HTML`). `.rtf` / `.txt` go through `file.exportText`. An unsupported extension is an error that names the extensions `--export` accepts.

**Actual**

`real.html` is 853 bytes of HTML. `via.html`, `via.rtf` and `via.txt` are identical 12935-byte PNG files (`PNG image data, 612 x 842`). Exit status 0. Stderr:

```text

title: Save writes the document in place, so a crash mid-save can destroy it
author: aiongg
body:
`file.save`, `file.saveAs` and `file.saveACopy` write the document with `std::fs::write(path, bytes)` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:30`, `:250`, `:523`). If the app is killed, the disk fills or a network volume drops mid-write, the existing file is truncated and the new one is incomplete, so the document is lost. Book, export, IDML, library, snippet and style writers do the same (`book.rs`, `export.rs`, `interchange.rs`, `library.rs`, `style.rs`, `xml.rs`).

**Expected:** write to a temporary file in the same folder, flush it to disk, rename it over the target, then flush the folder. If any step fails, the original file is untouched.

title: Feature request: story-level check-out, auto-save and version history on storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone)
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
InDesign teams collaborate through InCopy's managed files (check-out/check-in of stories with lock files on shared storage) or through Adobe cloud documents. Please add an open equivalent: a central "Save target" for auto-save and version history, and **story-level check-out with expiring leases** so designers and editors can work on the same publication without Adobe's cloud. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry.

## How InDesign does it
- **InCopy managed files:** content is split into story files plus the layout. Checking out an item places a hidden `.idlk` lock file on the file system; checking in saves the story to a shared location where others can check it out. Closing a document with checked-out content prompts to check in. Adobe warns that if someone deletes a lock file and edits the content, you get the undesirable situation of two versions.
- **Cloud documents** (InDesign is listed among the supported apps) autosave, create a version at each autosave, and are shared by "invite to edit".

## What DesignCraft has today (README only)
Spreads, parent pages, threaded stories, IDML import/export, a documented native format, O(1) copy-on-write undo, a crash-recovery path, commands for everything (UI/CLI/control channel/MCP). The web build's Save downloads a file.

## Proposal
**Phase 0:** make the crash-recovery path a write-ahead journal with a recovery prompt, `file.autoSave` and atomic writes.
**Phase 1, Save target:** shared building blocks below. Store the document as a **manifest plus parts** (per spread, per story, resources) so syncing and merging are fine-grained; IDML remains the interchange format. Linked images become content-addressed assets, and "Package" can collect links to the target. Warn about fonts that are missing on the opening machine.
**Phase 2, versions:** snapshots, named versions ("sent to print"), restore, and a story-level diff.
**Phase 3, story-level check-out:** a lease per story (and per spread for layout) with TTL + he…

title: Window decorations and title bar inconsistent with VectorCraft / PhotoCraft
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
The window decorations and title bar handling in `designcraft` are inconsistent with the standard established in VectorCraft (PR #969) and PhotoCraft (PR #1903).

### Current Behavior
- On Windows and Linux, the application either does not draw client-side decorations/caption buttons or lacks consistent custom title bar handling.
- There is no option for users to toggle `System Title Bar` (native OS window decorations) in Preferences/User Interface.

### Desired Behavior
Standardize title bar and window decoration architecture to match VectorCraft:
1. Support custom client-side titlebar and window caption buttons (Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close) with edge resize zones.
2. Provide a `System Title Bar` preference under User Interface to allow users to switch back to native OS decorations on Windows/Linux if desired.
3. macOS retains native window buttons and fullsize content view.

title: IDML import ignores SameParaStyleSpacing, adding unwanted paragraph gaps
author: stjohnbuilds
body:
Environment: macOS; DesignCraft v0.4.0-based local build. Not retested on the latest official release.

An IDML contains consecutive paragraphs using the same style, with SameParaStyleSpacing explicitly set to zero. InDesign respects this, including empty paragraphs. DesignCraft instead applies ordinary before/after spacing, adding gaps and moving subsequent text and anchored objects.

To reproduce: import an IDML with this setting and compare consecutive same-style paragraphs, including an empty paragraph, against InDesign.

Expected: preserve and apply SameParaStyleSpacing, while retaining ordinary spacing at different-style boundaries.

A local fix added the property to the document model, IDML import/export and shared composition. Regression tests covering zero, numeric and Ignore values, empty paragraphs and round trips completed without failures.

Relevant files:
crates/doc/src/attrs.rs
crates/idml/src/import.rs
crates/idml/src/export.rs
crates/compose/src/lib.rs

title: IDML import loses saved image clipping paths, exposing opaque backgrounds
author: stjohnbuilds
body:
Environment: macOS; DesignCraft v0.4.0-based local build. Not retested on the latest official release.

A placed RGB image has a saved ClippingPathGeometry in the IDML. InDesign clips its background correctly. DesignCraft discards the clipping geometry and displays the opaque background, covering neighboring artwork and lettering.

To reproduce: import an IDML containing an opaque image with a saved clipping path, then compare canvas/PDF output with InDesign.

Expected: retain the saved clipping geometry and apply it under the image transform on both canvas and PDF export, without altering image pixels or stacking order.

A local fix preserved the clipping path, coordinate normalization and inversion through import, rendering and export. Regression tests and an actual-page comparison showed the background no longer covering neighboring lettering.

Relevant files:
crates/doc/src/item.rs
crates/idml/src/import.rs
crates/idml/src/export.rs
crates/render/src/lib.rs
crates/pdf/src/export.rs

Related: #381 handles image-level text wrapping. This report concerns the image's visible clipping, which is a separate problem.

title: IDML import discards custom text-wrap boundaries stored separately from frame geometry
author: stjohnbuilds
body:
Environment: macOS; DesignCraft v0.4.0-based local build. Not retested on the latest official release.

An IDML rectangle has a custom triangular wrap boundary stored in TextWrapPreference/Properties/PathGeometry. This boundary differs from the visible rectangle. DesignCraft discards it, so text wraps around the wrong area and subsequent text flow changes.

To reproduce: import an IDML with an independently edited wrap boundary and compare text flow against InDesign.

Expected: preserve the saved wrap path independently of the visible frame, transform it with the object and use it during composition.

A local fix is drafted in the document model, IDML import/export and shared composition. Regression tests were written but have NOT been run; the fix is not verified or installed. The examined source boundary has zero offsets; nonzero offsets remain unverified.

Relevant files:
crates/doc/src/item.rs
crates/idml/src/import.rs
crates/idml/src/export.rs
crates/compose/src/lib.rs

Related: #384 adds contour wrapping, but its inspected patch uses frame geometry rather than importing this separately saved custom boundary.

To rotate the spread view in Adobe InDesign without affecting the actual document orientation or print output, select the desired page or spread in the Pages panel and navigate to View > Rotate Spread.  You can choose to rotate the view 90° Clockwise, 90° Counterclockwise, or 180°.  A small rotation icon will appear next to the spread thumbnail in the Pages panel to indicate the active rotation.

title: Crash recovery: two running apps write over each other's unsaved documents
author: noah1400
body:
Every running DesignCraft keeps its recovery data in the same folder and names each entry by a counter that starts at 1 in every process (`NEXT_UID` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, `<uid>.designcraft` in `crates/engine/src/recovery.rs`). Nothing stops a second launch, so two running apps both write `1.designcraft`.

**Steps** (0.6.0, Linux; both apps on one profile):

1. Start DesignCraft, File › New, add a text frame that says "WINDOW A". Don't save.
2. Start DesignCraft a second time, File › New, add a text frame that says "WINDOW B". Don't save.
3. Wait for the recovery timer (30 s). The recovery folder holds one entry, `1.designcraft`.
4. Kill both (a crash, a power cut, the session ending).
5. Start DesignCraft.

**Result:** one recovered document, "WINDOW B". "WINDOW A" is gone.

**A second launch also takes the first one's data.** With only the first app running and its entry written, start the second: it opens the first app's unsaved document as a recovered one and removes the entry (`recovery::open`), although the first app is still running.

I ran both with `--control` on a profile set by `DESIGNCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` (`file.new`, then `frame.create` with the text), and ended the apps with SIGKILL.

**Expected:** each running app keeps its own recovery data. A starting app reopens what apps that have ended left behind and leaves a running app's alone.

I'm working on this.

title: Cross-story numbered lists make large documents extremely slow (open, repaint, typing, PDF export)
author: ramiroroig
body:
[prueba-lentitud-listas.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33306856/prueba-lentitud-listas.zip)

[prueba-lentitud-listas.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33306877/prueba-lentitud-listas.zip)

## Summary

Documents with **numbered lists that continue across stories** become extremely slow: opening them, every repaint and every keystroke take seconds, and PDF export takes tens of seconds. A real 30-page IDML (677 stories, 8 lists with *Continue Numbers across Stories*) took **69 s** to compose and **~2 s per keystroke**.

## Cause

`Document::list_start` (`crates/doc/src/notes.rs`) orders every story by the page of its first frame to find where a story's numbering starts. For each call it:

1. computes the sort key of all stories and then sorts them with `sort_by_key`, which recomputes the key on every comparison (~S·log S times);
2. each key calls `page_of_item`, which runs `Document::find` **twice** — a linear walk of every item on every spread;
3. resolves the paragraph styles of all earlier stories.

`compose::Cache::get` calls it **for every story and every named list** while building the cache signature — even on cache hits — so every repaint pays roughly `lists × stories × S·log S × items`. In a profile (`sample`), `designcraft_doc::edit::find_in` accounted for ~70 % of CPU time, called from `list_start → sort_by_key → page_of_item → find`.

`footnote_start` and `endnote_start` / `endnote_order` (`crates/doc/src/endnotes.rs`) follow the same pattern, so documents with many footnotes or endnotes are affected too (`endnote_start` is even called per paragraph during composition).

## How to reproduce

Attached: **`prueba-lentitud-listas.zip`**, containing `Prueba lentitud listas.designcraft` and the `designcraft-cli script` that generates it (`designcraft-cli script "Prueba lentitud listas.script" --save out.designcraft`). The document is synthetic: 30 pages, 8 named lists with *Continue Numbers across Stories*, 600 text frames (3 numbere…

title: Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar: lines break mid-word and justification tears marks off their letters
author: visarutforthaipbs
body:

Thai (and Lao, Khmer, Myanmar) text is written without spaces between words. The composer only breaks at spaces/hyphens/CJK pairs, so a Thai paragraph is one giant "word": lines are split by the emergency path **in the middle of words and syllables**, and in justified text the Single-Word-Justification path letter-spaces every glyph gap, **tearing combining vowels and tone marks off their base consonants**.

Measured on v0.6.0 with a 30-paragraph corpus scored against PyThaiNLP `newmm` word boundaries ([harness + corpus](https://github.com/visarutforthaipbs/designcraft-thai-eval)): **38 of 106 line wraps (36%) are mid-word**, e.g. `เกณ|ฑ์`, `เปลี่|ยน`, `แบตเ|ตอรี่`, `สาธารณ|ะ`.

file.new {"preset":"A6","margins":24}
frame.create {"rect":[24,24,274,380],"content":"text","text":"ผู้ซื้อสามารถตรวจสอบประวัติเครื่องได้ทุกขั้นตอนโดยร้านจะบันทึกผลการตรวจสอบแบตเตอรี่หน้าจอคีย์บอร์ดและสถานะการล็อกไว้อย่างละเอียดก่อนส่งมอบให้ลูกค้าทุกครั้ง"}
selection.set {"ids":["$1.id"]}
type.char {"attrs":{"fontFamily":"Thonburi","size":14}}
type.para {"attrs":{"align":"leftJustified"}}
EOS
designcraft-cli run --in t.designcraft --page 0 --scale 2 --export t.png
```
Expected: lines end only between words (ขั้นตอน, แบตเตอรี่, อย่าง stay whole), marks never move.
Actual (0.6.0):

![0.6.0 contact sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/visarutforthaipbs/designcraft-thai-eval/main/out/0.6.0/contact.png)

title: IDML: custom anchored objects ignore their object style's anchor settings and misplace X
author: aiongg
body:
An anchored object whose `AnchoredObjectSetting` lists only some attributes (for example `AnchoredPosition="Anchored"` with `AnchorXoffset`/`AnchorYoffset`) should take the rest from its object style (`[None]` included): anchor point, reference points, X/Y relative-to. The importer reads only the item's own setting, so the missing attributes fall back to "relative to the anchor, object centre", and the object lands far from where it belongs, often off the page.

The X offset of a custom anchored object also moves the object the wrong way.

Expected: inherited settings apply, and the object sits where the original layout puts it.

title: Footnotes after the first sit one descent too low
author: aiongg
body:
Each footnote's height is its last baseline plus its descent (`crates/compose/src/notes.rs` ~120), and notes stack by adding heights (~190), so every footnote after the first gets an extra descent: about 15 pt between 9 pt footnotes where 12 pt is expected. title: Linked .docx text files: Links panel status and update (InDesign parity)
author: thaynej
body:
InDesign can place Word documents as linked text files: the Links panel shows them as OK / Modified / Missing, and Update Link re-imports the changed document into the same story and frames. DesignCraft 0.6.0 imports a .docx once (`file.place`), but records no link, so a layout can't tell that its source changed.

**Request (InDesign parity only):**
- `file.place {…, link: true}` and a "Create links when placing text files" preference, recording the source path, a content hash, and the style map used.
- Placed text files listed in the Links panel and `links.list` with the same status as graphics.
- `links.update` re-imports a modified file into its story, keeping frames and threading and reapplying the saved style map. Like InDesign, local edits in that story are replaced, with a warning.
- Tracked changes import as `file.place` does today (as if accepted).

This would reuse the existing link machinery (`Asset.link`, linked stories).

**Possible follow-up, not part of this request:** an update that keeps local layout fixes by comparing paragraphs, which would go beyond InDesign. Happy to discuss separately.

Split out from #77, which also covers Markdown. I'd be glad to build this as a PR if it's welcome.

title: Feature Request: Add Tabs and Bullets & Numbering to Paragraph Styles
author: srikrishnanr72
body:
Description

DesignCraft's Paragraph Style Options currently lack some basic paragraph-formatting features available in Adobe InDesign. For professional document layout and typesetting, Tabs and Bullets and Numbering are essential features.

Please consider implementing the following features in Paragraph Style Options.

1. Tabs

Define left, center, right, and decimal tab stops.

Specify custom tab positions.

Support tab leaders, such as dots or other characters.

Apply tab settings through paragraph styles.

2. Bullets and Numbering

Enable bulleted and numbered paragraphs through paragraph styles.

Allow users to customize bullet characters and numbering formats.

Configure alignment, left indent, first-line indent, and tab position.

Support automatic numbering sequences and continuation across paragraphs.

Why these features are important

These are fundamental requirements for professional typesetting, especially for books, journals, reference lists, tables of contents, and structured documents. Without them, users must rely on manual spacing or workarounds, making formatting less consistent and automation more difficult.

Implementing these features would significantly improve DesignCraft's suitability for professional publishing workflows.

Thank you for your work on DesignCraft and for continuing to improve this open-source alternative.

title: Windows 11: dragging the window across monitors with different display scales grows it and crashes (winit 0.30.13 mixed-DPI drag)
author: msaulc
body:
## Summary

DesignCraft locks winit 0.30.13 without a winit patch, so it should have the Windows 11 mixed-DPI drag bug found in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#760, fix in storytold/gridcraft#761). Dragging the window across the boundary between monitors with different display scales makes it flip between the two scales and grow by their ratio.

**Expected effect in DesignCraft:** **a crash** (closes with unsaved work lost), the same as GridCraft's.

This comes from reading DesignCraft's code at its current `main`, not from a run of DesignCraft. GridCraft, on the same stack, was reproduced and fixed on hardware.

## What happens (measured in GridCraft)

Windows 11 24H2, a 3440×1440 monitor at 100 % next to a 3840×2400 panel at 250 %. Dragging the window from the 250 % panel toward the top edge of the 100 % monitor, client size per step: 3600×2250 → 1440×900 → 3600×2250 → **9048×5757**. GridCraft then crashed in wgpu's `Surface::configure`: `Requested was (9048, 5757), maximum extent for either dimension is 8192`.

## Cause

- **winit 0.30.13's `WM_DPICHANGED` handling during a live drag** (rust-windowing/winit#4041, #4600). winit replaces the rect Windows suggests with its own and nudges it back onto the monitor being left, which triggers another DPI change. winit master fixed this in 488c036a (#4341), but only for 0.31; eframe 0.36 needs 0.30.
- **Surface size limit:** DesignCraft uses eframe's default device request of exactly 8192 px and installs no wgpu uncaptured-error handler, so wgpu's validation error is fatal. A window stretched across monitors adding up to more than 8192 px crashes the same way, without any drag.

## Fix used in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#761)

1. Pin winit to the single commit of rust-windowing/winit#4694, its 0.30.x backport (+21/−34 lines on top of v0.30.13), with no vendored copy:
   ```toml
   [patch.crates-io]
   winit = { git = "https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit", rev = "39c4009c41e5977d779cf8a365792c8153ca77c5" }
   ```

title: Pages panel: double-clicking a parent always opens the first parent; every parent row stays highlighted
author: aiongg
body:
In a document with several parents (common in imported IDML files), the Pages panel can't open a chosen parent for editing.

- Double-clicking a parent row turns on parent editing but doesn't say which parent: `layout.parents.edit` takes only `{on}` (crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs:182-188) and the view refits to the slot nearest the old view centre, usually the first parent. Double-clicking "C-Parent" shows A-Parent.
- While parents are being edited, every parent row is drawn selected (`active = editing_parents && prefix.is_some()`, crates/ui-egui/src/panels/pages.rs:91), and clicking empty space in the panel doesn't leave parent editing.
- Parent rows always show a blank icon; only document pages get thumbnails (pages.rs:63-73).
- Rows, drag payloads and Apply Parent identify parents by prefix, and `parent_ref` returns the first prefix match (layout.rs:617), so with parents IMG-Parent and IMG-Half, applying IMG-Half applies IMG-Parent. An unknown parent name silently clears the page's parent (layout.rs:166).

Expected: double-clicking a parent shows that parent and highlights only its row; parents have thumbnails; parents with the same prefix stay distinct.

title: Autoflow ignores the page's columns (one full-width frame per page)
author: Nmarello
body:
**Version:** designcraft-cli 0.6.0 (macOS universal release), Apple M4.

Autoflow ignores the page's columns. On a two-column document, the frame it creates and the frames on every page it adds span the whole margin width as one column, so text runs straight across the gutter (95 characters a line on Letter in the repro below). InDesign's autoflow fills each column of the page.

```sh
python3 -c 'print(("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. " * 12 + "\n\n") * 40)' > long.txt
designcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'file.new={"preset":"Letter","pages":1,"columns":2,"gutter":18,"margins":54}' \
  --cmd 'file.place={"path":"long.txt","page":1,"autoflow":true}' \
  --export long.pdf
# {"overset":false,"pagesAdded":7,…}: every page holds one full-width frame
```

The result is the same with an explicit `rect` and with `.docx`/`.md` sources. The column guides are drawn correctly in the app, but the frames don't follow them.

**Expected:** one threaded frame per column on page 1 and on each added page (or a frame with the page's column count and gutter).

title: Placing a .docx drops list bullets and numbering
author: Nmarello
body:
**Version:** designcraft-cli 0.6.0 (macOS universal release), Apple M4.

Placing a Word document keeps its headings and paragraph styles but drops list bullets and numbering. The items come in as plain paragraphs.

```sh
printf '# Title\n\nIntro paragraph.\n\n- first item\n- second item\n\n1. step one\n2. step two\n' > list.md
pandoc list.md -o list.docx      # Word lists (numbering.xml) with bullets and decimal numbers
designcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'file.new={"preset":"Letter"}' \
  --cmd 'file.place={"path":"list.docx","page":1}' \
  --export list.pdf
pdftotext list.pdf -   # "first item", "step one" … with no bullets or numbers
```

`place.styles` reports the paragraph styles (`Body Text`, `First Paragraph`, `Compact`, `heading 1`), and the headings are styled correctly. Only the list formatting is lost.

**Expected:** Word's bullets and numbering arrive as bullets and numbering (InDesign's Word import keeps them as live lists, or converts them to text when asked).

title: Text in an oval or polygon text frame is set as if the frame were a rectangle
author: aiongg
body:
Text frames lay out their text in the frame's bounding box after inset (`Item::text_area()`, crates/doc/src/item.rs:1156, used by compose's frame specs), so converting a text frame to an ellipse or a polygon, or drawing text into one, leaves the lines running into the corners outside the shape.

Expected: each line's width follows the frame's shape (inset applied inside the outline), and the text reflows when the shape or size changes, as with a rectangular frame.

title: CLI/scripting: no way to create items on a parent spread
author: DanielGemm
body:
**Version:** designcraft-cli 0.7.1 (also 0.6.0), Windows 11
**Type:** feature request / gap in the command API

`frame.create` (and `file.place`, `line.create`, `path.create`) only target body spreads. There is no parameter that targets a parent spread, so parent pages can't be built from a script at all.

What I tried (each with and without `layout.parents.edit {"on":true}` first):

```
file.new {"width":2304,"height":1440,"pages":1,"facingPages":false}
layout.parents.edit {"on":true}
frame.create {"spread":"A-Parent","rect":[0,0,100,100]}   # accepted, but item lands on page 1
frame.create {"parent":"A-Parent","rect":[0,0,100,100]}   # accepted, `parent` ignored, page 1
frame.create {"spread":1,"rect":[0,0,100,100]}            # error: no such spread
frame.create {"spread":3,"rect":[0,0,100,100]}            # (3 = parent spread id) error: no such spread
document.inspect {}                                        # parents[0].items == 0 in every case
```

**Expected:** a way to address a parent, e.g. `frame.create {"parent":"A", ...}`, or a `layout.parents.activate {"parent":"A"}` that makes subsequent commands go to that parent. Unknown values such as `"spread":"A-Parent"` should be rejected instead of silently falling back to page 1.

**Workaround used:** build the items on scratch pages, then move `spreads[i].items` into `parents[i].items` in `document.json` and drop the scratch spreads. This works: the items render and `layout.overrideParentItems` works on them afterwards.

Context: I rebuilt a 46-page portfolio (from a PDF whose layout file was lost) headlessly via the CLI, with one parent per recurring layout. Apart from this gap, the CLI worked very well for that.

title: Parent "based on" parent (ParentInfo.basedOn) is stored but not composed; no command to set it
author: DanielGemm
body:
**Version:** designcraft-cli 0.7.1 (also 0.6.0), Windows 11
**Type:** bug + missing command

`ParentInfo` has a `basedOn` field (u64, the id of another parent spread). A document with it set loads without error, but the base parent's items are **not drawn** on pages that use the derived parent, neither on the canvas of the derived parent nor in PDF export. There is also no CLI command to set it (`layout.parents.new` only takes `prefix` and `name`).

### Repro
1. Run this script and save it:
```
file.new {"width":2304,"height":1440,"pages":4,"facingPages":false,"margins":0}
layout.parents.new {"prefix":"B","name":"Opening"}
frame.create {"spread":0,"rect":[0,0,500,500],"content":"unassigned"}
object.fill {"swatch":"[Black]","ids":["$2.id"]}
frame.create {"spread":1,"rect":[600,0,1100,500],"content":"unassigned"}
object.fill {"swatch":"[Black]","ids":["$4.id"]}
layout.pages.applyParent {"pages":[3],"parent":"B"}
```
2. In `document.json`, move `spreads[0].items` to `parents[0].items` (A) and `spreads[1].items` to `parents[1].items` (B), drop those two spreads, and set `parents[1].parent.basedOn = parents[0].id`. (This is needed because of #651: there is no CLI way to put items on a parent.)
3. `designcraft-cli run --in doc.designcraft --export out.pdf`

**Actual:** the page using B shows only B's rectangle (x 600–1100).
**Expected:** it shows A's rectangle (x 0–500) too, like InDesign's "Based on Parent".
Setting the `parent` key on B's parent *pages* to A's id (mirroring how body pages reference their parent) has no effect either.

- A page whose parent B has `basedOn = A` draws A's items, then B's items (B on top), then its own items. This holds on the canvas, in PDF export and in IDML export (as `BasedOn` on the MasterSpread).
- `layout.overrideParentItems` on such a page can override items that come from A.

title: CLI script: a UTF-8 BOM breaks the first command; `script` has no --help / syntax reference
author: DanielGemm
body:
**Version:** designcraft-cli 0.7.1 (also 0.6.0), Windows 11
**Type:** small bug + docs

### 1. BOM
A script file saved as "UTF-8 with BOM" fails on its first line. That is the default of many Windows tools, e.g. Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` / `Out-File`, and Notepad's "UTF-8 with BOM".

Repro (PowerShell 5.1):
```powershell
'file.new {"width":100,"height":100,"pages":1}' | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 repro.txt
designcraft-cli script repro.txt
```
**Actual:** `step 0 (...) failed: unknown command `﻿file.new``. The BOM becomes part of the command id.
**Expected:** a leading U+FEFF is stripped (for `script FILE`, `script -` and `script.run {text}`).

**Acceptance criteria:** the same script with and without BOM produces identical results. A unit test covers BOM + CRLF line endings.

### 2. Docs
`designcraft-cli script --help` → `unknown script option --help`. The line syntax is only discoverable from `describe script.run` ("command script lines (`command.id {json}`, JSON lines or a JSON array; `$N.path` refers to earlier results)").
It would help to document in `script --help` (and the README):
- that `$N` is the **0-based step index** and paths go through result fields and array indices (`$1.story`, `$3.ids.0`)
- that `\n` in text is a paragraph break and `\u000b` a forced line break
- that unknown parameters are silently ignored (see #651). Ideally they would be rejected; a `--strict` flag would also do.

body:
### Description

- PhotoCraft: storytold/photocraft#3333, PR storytold/photocraft#3521

### Requested behaviour

- Press on a checkbox and drag over its neighbours. Each checkbox that the pointer goes over takes the new state of the first one, until you release the button.
- A click toggles one checkbox, as before.
- A mixed (dash) checkbox stays as it is during a drag.

VectorCraft PR #1600 and PhotoCraft PR #3521 use the same design. A `drag_toggle` helper in the shared checkbox keeps the new state while the primary button is down.
