title: Preserve document colour profiles through import, save and reopen
author: skylartaylor
body:
Preserve a document's colour-profile association through import, save and reopen, and use that profile when displaying its CMYK swatches.

The review of storytold/craft-libs#39 identified this as separate from the shared ICC engine. The library now distinguishes exact built-in names from approximate stand-ins, and its example prefers actual ICC bytes. Those changes alone do not connect a document's profile to the application's swatch rendering or persistence.

Our earlier source review found swatch display using process-wide colour settings and no document-profile handling in the IDML importer/document model. The end-to-end import/save/reopen workflow has not been validated by our library test run.

### Remaining work

- [ ] Carry a document's imported profile association in its document state, retaining actual ICC bytes when available and the original profile identity when only a name is available.
- [ ] Preserve that association through native save/reopen. Keep the source CMYK values unchanged when merely opening or saving the document.
- [ ] Use the document profile for swatch display instead of silently substituting the process-wide working space. Prefer actual ICC bytes; make missing-profile handling and approximate name-based stand-ins explicit. In particular, do not substitute the fitted 330% profile for a 300% profile name.
- [ ] Add a small reproducible import/save/reopen test with known CMYK values and a controlled profile. Check the retained profile/bytes and source values, plus consistent display conversion before and after reopening.
- [ ] Check two documents with different profiles in the same application session so their swatches do not inherit each other's profile or the current global working-space selection.
- [ ] Validate the visible swatch workflow with that fixture and record the profile, rendering intent and black-point-compensation settings used.

title: Deleting the return between two table paragraphs drops a table and saves a file that won't reopen
author: noah1400
body:
### What happens
If a story has two tables in a row, pressing Backspace at the start of the second table's paragraph merges the two anchor paragraphs into one. The second table is silently removed, and the remaining paragraph holds two table anchors.

Saving works. Reopening the saved file fails:

```
not a DesignCraft document: story N: table T paragraph must hold exactly one anchor
```

Pasting a copied table right next to an existing table anchor breaks the same way. There the *existing* table is replaced by the pasted copy, so a different table's content is lost.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a text frame, insert a table (`table.insert`), put the caret at the end of the story and insert a second table. The story is now `Intro¶<A1>¶<A2>¶`.
2. Put the caret at the start of the second table's paragraph and press Backspace (`text.delete`).
3. The story is now `Intro¶<A1><A2>¶`, and only one table is left.
4. `file.save`, then `file.open` the same file → the error above.

Paste variant: select a table's anchor, `edit.copy`, put the caret right after the anchor, `edit.paste`. The result is the same: two anchors in one paragraph, the original table gone, and the file won't reopen.

### Cause
- `Story::delete` (`crates/doc/src/story.rs:336-342`) keeps only one table id (`first.or(last)`) when it merges paragraphs.
- `Story::insert_story` (`crates/doc/src/slice.rs:118-120`) overwrites the target paragraph's table.
- `fix_tables` (`crates/doc/src/table.rs:1014-1030`) only checks that a table paragraph contains *an* anchor. `check_tables` (`table.rs:1042`) requires *exactly one*.
- Saving doesn't validate. Loading does (`crates/format/src/lib.rs:128`), so the problem only shows up when the file is reopened.

### Expected
Every table anchor stays in its own paragraph with its own table. Backspace between two tables shouldn't merge them, and pasting a table next to another should put the pasted one in a new paragraph. A file that saves must reopen.

title: File › Open Recent and recent files on the start screen
author: PiMinusMax
body:
DesignCraft has no list of recently opened documents: every reopen goes through *Open…* (Cmd+O) and the file dialog. PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FilmCraft and EffectCraft already have one.

**Proposal** (same pattern as PhotoCraft/VectorCraft):
- `Prefs.recent_files: Vec<String>`, most recent first, next to the existing `recent_fonts` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`), persisted with the preferences and capped at a configurable count (Preferences › File Handling › *Recent Items to Display*, default 20).
- Updated on every successful open and *Save As…* (moved to the front, no duplicates). *Save a Copy…* and exports don't touch it.
- **File › Open Recent**: a dynamic submenu after *Open…* with the file names (full path as tooltip), a separator and *Clear Recent Files*; disabled when empty. UI command `app.openRecent {index}`, so the control channel and MCP reach it.
- **Start screen** (`chrome.rs`, below New file / Open): a "Recent files" section with the last few documents. A missing file is shown greyed out and says so on click instead of failing silently.
- Tests: order/dedup, cap, survives a restart, clear, a missing file gives an error and no panic (never-crash rules).

No wasm impact: the list stays empty on the web build.

I'm working on a PR for this.

title: IDML import reads arbitrary linked local paths and can embed unrelated file bytes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction or tests were run. No exploit or destructive testing was performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/interchange.rs:78–132](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/cmd/interchange.rs#L78-L132)
- [crates/idml/src/import.rs:2309–2338](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/idml/src/import.rs#L2309-L2338)

Candidate resolution begins with the raw document-supplied path, then calls std::fs::read. Graphic import stores returned bytes even when image sniffing fails.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Importing untrusted IDML on native platforms, including base64 import, can read a process-readable file referenced as a graphic. A later save/package can include those unrelated bytes and disclose them when shared. No automatic outbound transmission or independently exposed remote endpoint has been demonstrated.

## Recommended remediation
Make external-link reads an explicit trust decision. Confine package-relative resolution to a canonicalized approved root, including symlinks; do not silently try arbitrary raw paths.

## Suggested regression tests
Use disposable fixture files to cover approved relative links, absolute paths, traversal, symlink escape, base64 import, and non-image bytes. Related confinement request: #242.

title: Web Save clears dirty state even when download initiation fails
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction or tests were run. No exploit or destructive testing was performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [apps/designcraft-web/src/web.rs:143–176](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/apps/designcraft-web/src/web.rs#L143-L176)
- [crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:1518–1526](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs#L1518-L1526)
- [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:54–55](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L54-L55)

DownloadFn returns (), the browser service only logs download errors, and download_document unconditionally invokes file.saveAs afterward.

## Conditions and realistic impact
If Blob creation or a fallible DOM/download-initiation operation fails, no file is delivered but the document is marked saved. Closing it can lose edits. This is distinct from browser cancellation after successful initiation, which cannot generally be confirmed by an anchor-download API.

## Recommended remediation
Return Result from the download service; propagate initiation failures and retain dirty state. Describe successful initiation accurately rather than claiming confirmed disk persistence.

## Suggested regression tests
Inject a failing host download callback and assert error reporting, unchanged saved snapshot, and retained dirty state; also cover successful initiation.

title: script.run removes undo history for successful edits when a later step fails
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction or tests were run. No exploit or destructive testing was performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/scripts.rs:8–25](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/cmd/scripts.rs#L8-L25)
- [crates/engine/src/lib.rs:421–453](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L421-L453)

script.run truncates child undo entries before examining report.failed. A returned error exits execute_unguarded before its aggregate undo entry is recorded.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A script makes a successful edit and then fails. The successful prefix remains in the document without its undo entries; child commands may already have cleared redo.

## Recommended remediation
Either roll back the whole script transaction, including history, or retain one undoable successful-prefix transaction when reporting failure.

## Suggested regression tests
Through Session::execute, run frame.create followed by an unknown command. Assert complete rollback or one undo restoring pre-script document and selection. This is separate from duplicate undo entries already tracked in #406.

title: Native and IDML ZIP imports need actual decompressed-byte and entry-count budgets
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction or tests were run. No exploit or destructive testing was performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/format/src/lib.rs:88–125](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/format/src/lib.rs#L88-L125)
- [crates/idml/src/import.rs:64–79](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/idml/src/import.rs#L64-L79)

Native archive reads use unrestricted read_to_end. IDML decompresses and retains every non-directory member; limiting initial Vec capacity does not limit subsequent growth.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Archives with excessive expanded size, aggregate data, or member count can exhaust memory and terminate the app, losing unsaved work. This is a resource-bound defect; no crash payload was developed or executed.

## Recommended remediation
Enforce actual per-member and aggregate expanded-byte limits and entry-count limits before growing collections. Skip irrelevant IDML members before decompression. Do not trust ZIP advertised sizes alone.

## Suggested regression tests
Use small test budgets and bounded synthetic archives at limit and limit+1, including many members and irrelevant entries. Assert normal errors without allocating the full oversized content.

title: Untrusted table dimensions and text-frame column counts can cause excessive allocations

body:

title: DTD parameter-entity expansion has no byte or work budget
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction or tests were run. No exploit or destructive testing was performed.

- [crates/engine/src/dtd.rs:166–187](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/dtd.rs#L166-L187)

The implementation repeatedly applies whole-string replacements for up to eight passes. Each replacement can expand the text substantially, and each pass clones the previous text. A pass count is not an output-size bound.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Repeated or chained parameter entities can produce disproportionate memory and CPU consumption during DTD processing. No exhaustion payload was generated or run.

## Recommended remediation
Track expanded bytes and substitution work, reject cycles, and stop before an allocation exceeds the budget.

## Suggested regression tests
Small-budget tests for normal expansion, repeated references, cycles, and an expansion crossing the budget; assert normal rejection without process exhaustion.

title: Upgrade quick-xml 0.38.4: reachable RUSTSEC-2026-0194 attribute-check CPU exhaustion
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

Application consumers retain quick-xml 0.38.4. DOCX parsing iterates attributes with default duplicate checks, the affected API in https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0194.html . The fixed version is 0.41.0; a separate 0.41.0 lockfile entry does not upgrade these consumers.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Imported XML with many distinct attributes on a tag incurs quadratic duplicate-checking work and can stall synchronous parsing. A live OSV query against the lockfile confirmed the affected version; no benchmark or adversarial input was executed.

## Recommended remediation
Upgrade affected application consumers to quick-xml >=0.41.0 and retain independent input/work budgets. RUSTSEC-2026-0195 also matches the version, but first-party NsReader reachability was not found, so this report does not claim that second advisory is reachable.

## Suggested regression tests
Verify dependency resolution and retain duplicate-attribute correctness coverage; add bounded high-attribute-count input coverage.

- [crates/engine/src/recovery.rs:377–444](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/recovery.rs#L377-L444)
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:615–625](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L615-L625)

relock returns success for directories not in the managed-run registry; explicit directory saves/deletions still address files by process-local document UID. protect_retained_sources checks in-memory ownership, not all existing files.

## Recommended remediation
Apply persistent ownership/isolation to explicit directories; verify ownership before replacement or deletion.

## Suggested regression tests
Independent-process tests using disposable directories with colliding initial UIDs; retain both documents and reject deletion of unowned entries.

execute_unguarded captures only UID/document before running, then creates HistoryEntry with st.selection.clone() after the command.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Commands such as creating/selecting a new frame restore the prior document on Undo but can restore IDs absent from it or the wrong caret/range. This differs from redundant undo entries already tracked in #406.

title: Archive import silently treats corrupt embedded assets and optional XML parts as absent
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction/tests or destructive testing were performed.

## Source evidence and root cause

Native lookup/read failures become None; asset replacement is conditional. Shared DOCX/XLSX part loading returns Ok(None) after decompression/CRC/UTF-8 errors.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Present-but-corrupt embedded assets or optional styles/shared-string parts can disappear while load succeeds, and saving can make loss persistent. Empty data for a genuinely unresolved link is a separate valid state.

## Recommended remediation
Distinguish missing optional entries from corrupt present entries; propagate corruption or explicit actionable warnings. Distinguish unresolved links from missing embedded payloads.

## Suggested regression tests
Bounded fixtures with corrupt-present asset/styles/shared-string parts must not silently succeed; truly absent optional parts should preserve documented behavior.

When adopt_asset returns None, graphic references keep the old numeric ID; posters explicitly retain Some(p). Story remapping likewise leaves failed adoptions unchanged.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A source/snippet has a missing referenced asset while the destination contains another asset under that number. Placement displays an unrelated destination image instead of retaining a missing graphic. Valid source asset collisions are already handled.

## Recommended remediation
Reject unresolved references or remap to fresh missing-asset placeholders rather than preserving an ambiguous numeric ID.

## Suggested regression tests
Place a source with a dangling graphic/poster into a destination containing a distinct image under that ID; assert rejection or preserved missing state, never substitution.

title: XLSX import rounds numeric values to ten decimals and can overflow during formatting
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

title: Asset deduplication performs quadratic scans of distinct equal-size buffers
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction/tests or destructive testing were performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/format/src/lib.rs:110–120](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/format/src/lib.rs#L110-L120)
- [crates/doc/src/assets.rs:249–257](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/doc/src/assets.rs#L249-L257)

Format loading buckets buffers by length and compares every new buffer against previous candidates. Model deduplication similarly scans representatives grouped by length/MIME/page.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Many distinct equal-size assets, especially with long common prefixes, cause disproportionate CPU work while loading/saving. This is additional amplification beyond archive decompression.

## Recommended remediation
Index by a content digest plus relevant semantics and confirm equality within matching digest candidates; retain overall input/work budgets.

## Suggested regression tests
Use many distinct equal-size buffers with controlled common prefixes and check bounded comparison work, not fragile wall-clock assertions. This is narrower than the general image-performance report #566.

author: PierrunoYT
body:

Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/render/src/images.rs:24–34](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/render/src/images.rs#L24-L34)

The global negative cache retains strong Arc<Vec<u8>> values. Normal budget eviction covers successful pixmaps only, not failed entries.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Repeated distinct decode failures accumulate retained encoded bytes across renders until explicit cache clearing, independently of the pixmap budget.

## Recommended remediation
Bound negative-cache entries/retained bytes and evict or clear them with appropriate lifecycle rules.

## Suggested regression tests
Feed repeated distinct bounded invalid images and assert budget compliance and release of evicted buffers. Separate from saved-file asset compaction and general image performance in #566.

title: Printer discovery and submission synchronously wait without cancellation/deadlines
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High in the source-level defect. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction/tests or destructive testing were performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:244–246](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L244-L246)
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs:34–66](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/cmd/print.rs#L34-L66)

The UI synchronously calls printer discovery and submission. The pinned craft-print implementation waits for subprocess completion without a deadline: https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/blob/d991bf6792f8ade99c51358bf3c1d902c8cd96b5/crates/print/src/lib.rs#L350-L368 and #L544-L574 . Windows submission also waits synchronously at lines 467–483.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A stalled utility/spooler/driver can prevent the UI command from returning indefinitely. Normal pipe-buffer deadlock is already mitigated by concurrent feeding; no shell injection is claimed.

## Recommended remediation
Move operations to a cancellable worker with deadlines; terminate/reap children and coordinate feeder/tempfile ownership on cancellation.

## Suggested regression tests
Use non-printing stand-in children that stall before reading and before exiting; assert bounded return, child reaping, feeder completion and temporary-file cleanup.

author: PierrunoYT
body:

- [crates/images/src/eps.rs:26–48](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/images/src/eps.rs#L26-L48)

title: Investigate serialization-error path: to_bytes returns empty bytes that save treats as success
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** Potential High; practical failure trigger not established. **Confidence:** High for the error-handling path, not for ordinary-document reachability. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction/tests or destructive testing were performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:112–114](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L112-L114)
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:236–263](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L236-L263)
- [crates/format/src/lib.rs:58–75](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/format/src/lib.rs#L58-L75)

to_bytes uses designcraft_format::save(d).unwrap_or_default(). file_save then writes those bytes, marks the document saved and discards recovery. The serializer returns Result for its JSON/ZIP operations.

## Conditions and realistic impact
If serialization returns Err, atomic replacement can install an empty file while the command reports success. The audit did not establish a practical normal-document input that makes this in-memory serializer return Err. This is a conditional error-path finding, not a demonstrated file-loss reproduction.

## Recommended remediation
Return Result from to_bytes and propagate errors through callers; do not equate an empty fallback with successful serialization.

## Suggested regression tests
Use controlled serializer failure injection and assert unchanged prior file, saved snapshot, dirty state and recovery. Establish reachable error cases separately without causing actual data loss.

title: Panic guard does not roll back history or switched/multiple-document session state
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** Medium; conditional on a panic after partial mutation. **Confidence:** High for the rollback gap. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction/tests or destructive testing were performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/engine/src/guard.rs:35–58](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/guard.rs#L35-L58)
- [crates/engine/src/guard.rs:70–87](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/engine/src/guard.rs#L70-L87)

guarded snapshots only active UID/document/selection/revision and restores only if that UID remains active. History, redo, journal and document collection changes are not restored. The existing synthetic test performs a nested edit before panic but only asserts document restoration.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A nested successful edit followed by panic can leave history inconsistent with restored content; switching active documents can skip document restoration entirely. No newly discovered naturally occurring panic trigger is claimed.

## Recommended remediation
Define and restore the full command transaction state, including history and document identity/collection changes, or narrow and enforce the mutation contract.

## Suggested regression tests
Extend synthetic panic coverage to nested commands, redo/journal, document switch/create/close and selection. Verify all observable state after the error, not only Arc identity.

title: Verify final PDF/A conformance after post-validation forms/media updates
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686) (0.7.1), verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** Medium; final conformance requires independent validation. **Confidence:** High for source ordering; output conformance not runtime-tested. Rust/Cargo were unavailable; no runtime reproduction/tests or destructive testing were performed.

## Source evidence and root cause
- [crates/pdf/src/export.rs:104–115](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/pdf/src/export.rs#L104-L115)
- [crates/pdf/src/export.rs:210–227](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/pdf/src/export.rs#L210-L227)

PDF/A-2b configures the archival validator, then pdf.finish completes validation. Fields/media are subsequently appended through forms::add_fields. Only PDF/X excludes these additions.

## Conditions and realistic impact
PDF/A export with media enabled can acquire archival-incompatible multimedia after validation. This report establishes the ordering/policy gap; it does not claim that an external validator was run or that all added forms are inherently prohibited.

## Recommended remediation
Restrict postprocessing by standard and validate final emitted bytes, not just the pre-update document. Reject/omit incompatible features with clear diagnostics.

## Suggested regression tests
Export a bounded PDF/A fixture with media enabled and validate final bytes using an independent conformance checker. Include media-disabled and supported-form controls.

title: Public API hardening: validate dimensions, recursion progress and payload preservation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Audit baseline and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main [e862e0a](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/commit/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686), version 0.7.1, verified current on 2026-10-13.

**Severity:** Medium at the public-library boundary. **Confidence:** High in the cited source paths; ordinary application reachability varies and is qualified below. Rust/Cargo were unavailable. No runtime tests, exploit development, or destructive testing were performed.

This checklist groups API-hardening findings that should not be represented as demonstrated ordinary-user exploits. Each item includes its own conditions, impact, remediation and suggested test.

- [ ] **Trace input validation and recursive progress.** [`crates/geom/src/trace.rs:11–12,79–98`](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/geom/src/trace.rs#L11-L98) indexes a mask using unchecked dimensions. A short mask panics. With negative/NaN tolerance, collinear simplification can leave `idx=0` and recurse on the unchanged slice. The application clipping command clamps tolerance, so that route does not establish exposure to invalid tolerance. Validate checked mask size and finite nonnegative tolerance and guarantee progress. Test short masks and invalid tolerances through `trace` with bounded inputs.
- [ ] **Rendered PNG size validation.** [`crates/render/src/lib.rs:49–52,69–75`](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/e862e0a613c0793c6fea7cfd37ad4145ed6cf686/crates/render/src/lib.rs#L49-L75) exposes dimensions/pixels publicly and multiplies/resizes before `from_raw` can reject. Invalid direct callers can overflow or request excessive allocation. Normal renderer caps mitigate its usual path. Use checked size computation, a pixel budget and fallible allocation before conversion. Test oversize rejection without actually allocating oversized buffers.
- [ ] **PDF postprocessor checked ranges.** [`crates/pdf/src/transitions.rs…

title: Scripts: a GREP replacement that starts with `$1` is read as a step reference
author: aiongg
body:
### What happens
In a `designcraft-cli script` file (and the Scripts panel), any string parameter that starts with `$` is taken as a reference to an earlier step's result. A GREP replacement such as `$1` followed by a nonbreaking space fails the whole script:

```
frame.create {"rect":[36,36,400,400],"content":"text","text":"a v Praze"}
find.change {"find":"\\b([aikosuvz]) ","change":"$1 ","grep":true,"caseSensitive":true}
```

```
bad reference `$1 `
```

The same step works when sent directly to `find.change`, so GREP backreferences at the start of a replacement can't be used from scripts.

### Expected
Only a string made entirely of a well-formed reference (`$N`, `$N.path`, `$last…`) is replaced. Anything else stays literal text, and `$$` writes a literal `$`. The script help documents both.

title: Find/Change: save and reuse queries
author: aiongg
body:
Find/Change has no way to keep a search. Every GREP or text query (pattern, replacement, options, formats) has to be typed again each time, which makes recurring clean-up passes hard, for example the Czech and Slovak rule that keeps one-letter prepositions and conjunctions (a, i, k, o, s, u, v, z) with the next word through a nonbreaking space.

### Expected
- A Query menu at the top of the Find/Change window lists saved queries; choosing one fills in the find and change fields, the GREP or Text mode, the options and the formats.
- Save Query (asks for a name) and Delete Query next to it.
- Saved queries persist across sessions and are available to every document.
- A command for each action, so scripts, the control channel and MCP can list, run and save queries.

title: Preferences OK panics when the dialog has horizontalUnits but no verticalUnits
author: noah1400
body:
**What happens**
Confirming the Preferences dialog panics with "no entry found for key" when its fields hold `horizontalUnits` but no `verticalUnits`. The panic is on the UI thread and outside the crash guard, so the app exits. The never-crash rule says input from the control channel must not do that.

**Steps** (main e862e0a, `designcraft --sample --control 7979`)
```
{"id":1,"method":"ui.dialog.open","params":{"id":"preferences","fields":{"horizontalUnits":"points"}}}
{"id":2,"method":"ui.dialog.confirm"}
```
The first request answers ok. The second gets `{"error":"timeout","id":2,"ok":false}`, the connection closes and the process exits with status 101:
```
thread 'main' panicked at crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:2040:107:
no entry found for key
```
With `verticalUnits` in the fields as well, the same confirm gets a normal reply (an error about another missing field) and the app keeps running.

**Cause**
The Preferences branch of `dialogs::confirm` checks only that `horizontalUnits` is there and then indexes both `d.fields["horizontalUnits"]` and `d.fields["verticalUnits"]`. Indexing a `serde_json::Map` panics on a missing key. Edit › Preferences always fills both, so it takes a caller that passes its own `fields` to `ui.dialog.open`.

**Expected**
No panic. A field that is missing leaves its setting as it is.

I'm working on this.

title: Adding a drop shadow changes the colours of every other object on the spread
author: PiMinusMax
body:
**What happens:** In a print document (A4, Letter, …), applying a drop shadow to one object changes how *all other* objects on the spread look on screen. A placed photo that doesn't touch the shadow gets lighter in the dark areas and duller overall. Saturated fills shift too. Removing the shadow brings the original colours back.

**Steps:**
1. File › New, A4 (intent Print).
2. Place a dark RGB photo (a night shot shows it best).
3. Draw a rectangle next to it, give it a fill, and apply Object › Effects › Drop Shadow.

Pixels on screen at the same points of the photo, far from the shadow:

| | no shadow | with shadow | with shadow, Edit › Transparency Blend Space › Document RGB |
|---|---|---|---|
| dark area | 9, 10, 8 | 15, 14, 12 | 9, 10, 8 |
| leaf | 47, 34, 6 | 49, 37, 10 | 47, 34, 6 |
| cyan fill of the rectangle | 0, 159, 227 | 0, 154, 215 | 0, 159, 227 |

**Why:** In `Renderer::render` (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`, `blend_space_view`), when the blend space is CMYK and *any* item on a spread involves transparency, the whole spread is run through the working CMYK profile and back. The canvas turns this on whenever Proof Colors is off (`blend_space_view: !app.ui.proof_colors` in `canvas.rs`). The shadow is only the switch. The photo itself is converted the same way at output with or without the shadow, so its printed result doesn't change. Only the screen does.

**Expected:** With View › Proof Colors off, the canvas shows the document in RGB, the same way whether or not something on the spread is transparent. Simulating print belongs to View › Proof Colors (Proof Setup › Working CMYK), which already converts the whole view. That keeps the preview when someone asks for it, and nothing jumps when an effect is added. Export is unaffected: the blend space still applies to PDF output.

Making the canvas follow this is a small change: don't set `blend_space_view` from the canvas (or drop it). #588 extends the same on-screen CMYK path to blend modes and would need the s…

title: Support external links in native .designcraft saves instead of always embedding linked artwork
author: ForestParks
body:
## Workflow problem

Native `.designcraft` saves embed placed artwork even when the asset already has an external link. Please support keeping artwork externally linked in native working documents, with embedding available as an explicit choice.

This is a focused follow-up to the linked-save request in the closed #391. It concerns external-link storage, rather than duplicate placements or unused-resource cleanup. Related: #566 and #340.

## Public implementation evidence

At v0.7.1, [crates/format/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/v0.7.1/crates/format/src/lib.rs) documents native ZIP files containing `assets/<id>.<ext>`. The native save implementation writes referenced nonempty asset data into those entries even when an external link is retained.

The native `file.save` / `file.saveAs` command interfaces expose a path but no linked-only storage option. In contrast, IDML export has an `embedImages:false` option.

I understand embedding is currently intentional. The issue is the missing native linked-only mode, which prevents a normal external-link working-document workflow.

## Generic reproduction

title: IDML: liquid layout settings aren't read or written
author: aiongg
body:
IDML import and export drop all liquid layout data. The native format keeps it.

- Page rule (Off, Scale, Re-center, Guide-based, Object-based, Controlled by Parent): import sets every page to the default; export writes nothing.
- Object pins and resize locks for object-based pages: not mapped.
- Liquid guides: imported and exported as ordinary guides.
- `crates/idml/src/lib.rs` lists liquid layout as unsupported.

Steps: set a page to Object-based, pin an object, add a liquid guide, export IDML and open it again. All three settings are gone.

The open Page tool and Liquid Layout PRs (#862, #864, #866, #867, #868) add more of these settings, so the gap grows with them.

title: Master page enhancements: Page numbering tool, center spine guide for spreads, and responsive Properties panel
author: lt-cao
body:
Summary
When working with Master pages (Parent pages) and multi-page layouts, several core editorial design features are currently missing or present usability issues:

2. Missing Center Spine Line (Gutter Guide) in Two-Page Spreads**
   - Current behavior:** In two-page spread view, there is no visual center spine divider line indicating where the pages fold/split.

3. Properties Panel Overlaps Content on Small Screen Scaling
   - Current behavior:** Scaling down the window or zoom level causes the floating/fixed "Properties" panel to overlap and obscure the canvas content.
   - Expected: Make the Properties panel responsive, dockable, or auto-collapse so it does not block the workspace when scaled down.

 Expected Benefit
- Complete support for standard editorial publishing workflows (magazines, books, brochures).
- Improved visual guidance during spread layout design.
- Cleaner workspace UI adaptivity across various screen resolutions and zoom levels.

title: Transform (scale and shear) logic
author: andrestelex
body: Scaling an object scales its properties, but its properties values are not updated. Scaling happens by using the scale inputs in the Transform panel or by dragging object handles by pressing Ctrl/Cmd This create misleading values that are hard to track for users. If multiple objects are scaled (intentionaly or mistakenly), the user can hardly track if the values that the selections shows are accurate. Width and height properties currently show the object dimensions, so they 'reload' on scaling. The same should happen with other measures. ### Objects When an object with a stroke is scaled, the stroke thickness is scaled as well. But the property of the stroke remains the same. If we have a square with 1px stroke, when scaling 500%, the stroke gets thicker. But the property of the stroke remains 1pt. Object properties that represent a measurement shouldn't be relative, but absolute. ### Text frames When scaling a text frame, the point size and leading remain relative. So the panels will indicate that a text has a specific point size (or other point values). But that is misleading, because there is a scaling value on top. Scaling a text frame should update it's properties. If the frame ratio is not constrained (for example, by scaling height only) the text properties related to point size or leading should update based on the height. Changing only the width of a text frame shouldn't change typesetting measurements (point size and leading relate to vertical measurements). Special attention should be taken when scaling Vertical Text: the opposite happens and scaling by width will change the point size. ### Shear Shear shows a logic on transformation that is not ideal, also by shearing (slanting) the fi…

title: [Feature request] Better sort font styles
author: andrestelex
body:
The application might expose to the user the methods to sort font styles.
Different applications have different methods. Designcraft could have its own default method (whatever it is right now that seems to be by weight first, then width, then italics) but have configuration options that allow users to decide how to sort font styles.
Font styles could be sorted by os2WidthClass, os2WeightClass, italic (postItalicAngle, name id 2 = italic), panose, etc.
It would be great if the way this is performed is accessible to designers and font developers.

title: [Feature request] Character panel styles with filter (string or properties filter)
author: andrestelex
body:
In the same way that in the Font select we can filter the font family name to find the desired one, the Style select can do.
Modern fonts, especially Variable fonts, can have multiple styles, sometimes over hundreds. Long style menus (and its sorting) make really hard to select the desired styles or instances.
The style menu can filter by name, so the user can quickly access a style by it's name. For example by typing 'Disp' will filter immediatly to the Display styles, or 'Condensed' to access all the styles including that string in the name.

This could be pushed even further, by having some filter submenu that could make use of isVariable, weight range, os2weightClass, os2WidthClass, italic angle, panose values, etc. so the user could filter based on some font properties (design properties or even information like vendor, designer, etc)

Some interesting font classification was proposed here but it's not yet implemented
https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/466

Designcraft could get the lead in using font information to display fonts and styles in a flexible and accessible way, which most applications don't.

**Expected:** PDF/X-4 requires every font used to be embedded, so the export should embed a substitute, convert the text to outlines, or fail with a message; `validate-pdf` should report an unembedded font. In the real job below, InDesign's PDF has 0 unembedded fonts.

title: Colour parsing: CMYK values that are all 1 or less are read as fractions, so a 1% cyan tint exports as 100% cyan
author: director-LAC
body:
**Version:** designcraft-cli 0.7.1, main 43a46c0 (built 2026-10-14), Linux x86_64. Also seen on 3384224 and e862e0a.

Follow-up to #510 (597f0e6), which fixed the mixed case: `{"c": 0.7, "m": 0, "y": 12.2, "k": 0}` exports `0.007843138 0 0.12156863 0 k`.

The all-small case is still ambiguous. `swatch.create {"name": "Tint1", "color": {"c": 1, "m": 0, "y": 0, "k": 0}}`, applied with `object.fill` and exported with `file.exportPdf`, writes `1 0 0 0 k`, so a 1% cyan tint prints as 100% cyan. The same happens for any light tint where every component is 1 or less (for example C 0.5 M 0.5 Y 0 K 0). In print work these are real values (paper-tone tints, light screens), and the error is silent and expensive.

Suggestion: treat CMYK as percentages 0 to 100 always (as InDesign's scripting DOM does), or add an explicit unit (`"scale": "percent" | "fraction"`) and reject ambiguous input without one. A warning in the command result when every component is 1 or less would also help.

Minor: CMYK values appear to be stored in 1/255 steps (0.7% exported as 0.784%, 12.2% as 12.157%, 50% as 50.196%). Not a problem for us at those values, but full-precision floats would match InDesign output more closely.

**Control:** in the same probe, `{"c": 50, "m": 0, "y": 0, "k": 0}` exports `0.5019608 0 0 0 k`.

**Why it matters for print:** light tints silently become solid ink; a 1% cyan paper tone prints as 100% cyan.

I understand from #510 that "every component within 0..1 means fractions" is kept so the older fraction form still works; the trouble is that the same input is a valid and common percentage in print.

title: Place puts the graphic on the first page while a parent page is open
author: aiongg
body:
With a parent page open and no frame selected, File › Place adds the graphic to the first document spread instead of the parent. Dropping a file onto the window does the same. Reported on Discord for PNG and SVG on 0.8.0.

title: Open INDD books (.indb): convert the chapters to a .dcbook
author: aiongg
body:
A book file (`.indb`) can't be opened. Its chapters are INDD files, which DesignCraft can read (through indd-utils) but not write, so a `.dcbook` can't keep them as chapters. Converting the chapters to IDML first doesn't help: `book.paginate` and `book.syncStyles` refuse imported IDML chapters.

Proposal:
- indd-utils reads the book: the chapters in order and the style source (page-numbering options later).
- File › Import Book (.indb)… asks for a destination folder, converts each chapter to `<chapter>.designcraft` there, and writes a `.dcbook` with the same chapter order and style source.
- Chapter paths in a `.indb` are absolute paths from the author's machine. When one isn't found, it tries the same file name next to the `.indb`, then the relative path. A report lists chapters it couldn't find and each chapter's import warnings.
- It never overwrites an existing file without asking and never changes the `.indb` or `.indd` files.

title: IDML import: a placed SVG whose art overhangs its viewBox is stretched onto its GraphicBounds
author: kenny-t-vo
body:
**DesignCraft 0.8.0** (macOS universal).

The SVG here has only a viewBox, as Illustrator exports them, and its art reaches past the viewBox. When InDesign places such an SVG, it writes the art's bounds as the graphic's `GraphicBounds`, in viewBox units: `-11 0 200 100` for a 200 × 100 viewBox here. It still draws the viewBox at one unit to the point. DesignCraft stretches the viewBox onto the GraphicBounds instead, so the whole graphic, text included, is scaled by 211/200 and moved.

**Repro.** InDesign 2026 (21.4.1) placed `overhang.svg` and `inside.svg` (below) on a Letter page, their frames' left edges at x 206 pt, and exported `svg-overhang.idml` (below, base64). I changed one thing in it: its two links are rewritten to the SVGs' bare names. Both SVGs have `viewBox="0 0 200 100"`, "A" at x 20 and "B" at x 170; `overhang.svg` adds a line reaching 10 units left of the viewBox.

```
base64 -d svg-overhang.idml.b64 > svg-overhang.idml    # beside overhang.svg and inside.svg
designcraft-cli run --in svg-overhang.idml --export out.pdf
pdftotext -bbox out.pdf -
```

| | overhang.svg: A, B (xMin, pt) | its glyph width | inside.svg: A, B |
|---|---|---|---|
| InDesign 2026, its own PDF | 237, 387 | 16.01 | 226, 376 |
| DesignCraft 0.8.0 | 227.1, 385.35 | 16.89 | 226, 376 |

- **Expected:** `overhang.svg` drawn as InDesign draws it: the viewBox at one unit to the point, its origin 11 pt in from the frame's left edge, where GraphicBounds' Left puts it.
- **In the code:** `graphic` in `crates/idml/src/import.rs` (lines 2316–2334 at v0.8.0) takes the size from `GraphicBounds` and offsets by `(l, t)`: `size = ((r - l).abs(), (b - t).abs())`, `xf: gxf * Affine::translate((l, t))`. It then draws the SVG's viewBox into that size. When the art stays inside the viewBox, the two agree.
- With `width` and `height` on the `<svg>`, InDesign stretches too. An IDML giving such an SVG GraphicBounds of `-10 0 200 100` draws A at 217 in both apps. So the difference is in SVGs with only a …

title: Text frame auto-size (heightOnly) never resizes the frame, so imported IDML captions come in blank
author: b662gftnpj-code
body:
**Version:** DesignCraft 0.8.0 and designcraft-cli 0.8.0 (macOS universal release). Same result headless (`mcp`) and in the app (`mcp --connect`).

## What happens

A text frame with `autoSize: heightOnly` keeps its height whatever its text needs. A frame too short for its text stays short and sets nothing, and a frame taller than its text does not shrink.

In an IDML from InDesign 2026 this blanks every caption: InDesign's caption frames are one line tall with `AutoSizingType="HeightOnly"` and grow to fit. DesignCraft keeps them 15.6 pt tall, sets 0 lines, and preflight reports each one as overset. In one 36-page report that is 62 overset errors, every one a caption or figure label, and none of them visible.

## Steps (headless)

```text
new_document  {"width": 841.89, "height": 595.28, "margins": 42.52}
execute  {"command": "frame.create", "params": {"spread": 0, "rect": [553.43, 227.73, 794.37, 243.35], "content": "text",
          "text": "Figure 1. A caption long enough to need two lines at this size, so the frame has to grow to show it."}}
get_story  {"frame": <id>}            → lines: 0, frame height 15.6

title: Tables: "Fit to frame width" option so a table follows its frame's width
author: switch87
body:
**Wish:** a table option that keeps the table at 100% of its text frame's width. When the frame (or its text column) gets wider or narrower, the columns scale proportionally so the table always spans the full measure.

**Evidence:** the InDesign team asked users what to improve in tables (https://redd.it/1luvoma, 111 points, 130 comments). The second-highest reply (134 points) asks to "lock a table to 100% of the frame width"; today you have to redistribute the columns by hand after every frame resize.

**Current state:** DesignCraft already scales a table *down* when it is wider than the column (`compose/src/table.rs`), but never up, and there is no option to make the table follow the frame.

**Proposal:**
- `TableOptions` gets a `fit_to_frame` flag (saved in the document, default off, old files load unchanged).
- When set, composition scales the stored column widths by `available width / natural width` in both directions; the stored widths act as proportions, so the table follows every frame resize.
- `table.options` takes `fitToFrame: bool`, `table.get` reports it, and the Table panel gets a "Fit to frame width" checkbox.
- InDesign has no equivalent table attribute, so this is a DesignCraft-only option: IDML export leaves it out (the exported column widths are the stored ones), and this is documented.

I'm working on this.

title: [Audit] 4 defects with evidence and fix PRs: IDML CJK metrics refuse the file, save writes an unloadable document, DOCX off imports as on, DOS EPS TIFF preview offsets
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Round-4 audit: 4 defects found on current `main` (a930276), each with an independent fix PR carrying a regression test that fails on `main` and passes on the branch.

### 1. One unusable IDML CJK metric makes the whole file unopenable — data loss
Composite-font and mojikumi metrics are taken from the file with no sanity check (`crates/idml/src/import.rs:502`, `:536`), while `Document::check()` refuses a zero/non-finite `relative_size`/`horizontal_scale`/`vertical_scale`/`baseline_shift` (`crates/doc/src/lib.rs:734`) and `import_idml` runs that check on the finished document. `RelativeSize="0"` or `BaselineShift="NaN"` on one entry anywhere in the package fails the whole import with *"invalid composite font metrics"*.
**Fix:** #1027

### 2. A saved `.designcraft` file can be one the app can no longer open — data loss
`format::save` never reads its bytes back; serde_json writes a non-finite `f64` as `null`, which a coordinate can't deserialize from. `file.place` with `{"x":1e308,"width":1e308}` computes `x + bw*k` to infinity in the item's path anchors (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:370` — unlike `guides.rs`/`flex.rs`, no finiteness filter), `file.save` writes the archive, reports success, and deletes the recovery copy; the next `load` rejects the file the app itself just wrote.
**Fix:** #1028 (the complementary entry-point filters and a fallible `to_bytes` are a wider policy change, left to the maintainers)

### 3. Word's `off` imports as `on` — silent mis-import
`ST_OnOff` (ECMA-376 §17.17.4) includes the words `on`/`off`, but the toggle reader only counts `0/false/none` as off (`crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:50`, underline `:170`), so `<w:b w:val="off"/>` (LibreOffice/POI and Word-2003-XML writers) imports bold — same for `w:i`, `w:strike`, `w:caps`, `w:isLgl`, `w:u`.
**Fix:** #1029

### 4. The DOS EPS TIFF preview is read from the wrong header offsets — documented feature never fires
The EPSF binary header is 22 bytes; `tiffStart`/`tiffLength` live at 12/16, but …

title: The DOS EPS TIFF preview is read from the wrong header offsets and never used
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The EPSF binary header is 22 bytes; `tiffStart`/`tiffLength` live at 12/16, but `crates/images/src/eps.rs:20` reads 20/24 (the checksum plus `"%!"`, always past EOF). A fifth lead (transparency-flattener spread branch holding every page raster at flatten ppi 1200 — ~5.4 GB before encoding on a ten-page book) is recorded for the maintainers' judgment rather than filed as a finding: the right bound (cap, warn, clamp ppi, or stream per page) is a product decision.

title: Windows: crash recovery is always off ("this run no longer owns its recovery lock"), and every start leaves a run folder behind
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version / OS:** DesignCraft 0.8.0 windows-x64 portable, Windows 11 (10.0.26200), NVIDIA RTX 3060. Same code on `main` (a930276).

### Steps
1. Start DesignCraft (no document needed). Started from Explorer, so nothing special about the environment.
2. Look at `%APPDATA%\DesignCraft\logs\designcraft.log`.

### Expected
This run gets its own recovery folder `%APPDATA%\DesignCraft\Recovery\run-<pid>-0` and recovery is on.

### Actual
On every start:

```
WARN  [main] designcraft::profile: recovery is unavailable because this run cannot be isolated: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\DesignCraft\Recovery\run-23896-0\lock: this run no longer owns its recovery lock
```

So crash recovery never runs on Windows. The folder is also left behind (it still holds the `lock` file, so `remove_dir` fails): after 2 starts from Explorer there were 2 `run-<pid>-0` folders, after a test series of 10 starts, 10.

### Likely cause
`crates/engine/src/recovery.rs`, `run_dir` → `validate_lock` (added in 328b4d5, "isolate recovery data between app instances"): the run takes `lock.try_lock()` (an exclusive `LockFileEx` over the whole file on Windows), then opens the lock file again by name and reads its marker through that second handle (`lock_marker(&named)`). On Windows byte-range locks are mandatory, so that read fails with `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION` and `validate_lock` returns "no longer owns its recovery lock". The read through the locking handle itself (`lock_marker(lock)`, a `try_clone` of the same handle) works.

A minimal check of the Windows behaviour in PowerShell (.NET `FileStream.Lock` is `LockFileEx` as well):

```powershell
$fs = [IO.File]::Open("$env:TEMP\t.lock", 'Create', 'ReadWrite', 'ReadWrite')
$fs.Write([byte[]](49,50,51), 0, 3); $fs.Flush(); $fs.Lock(0, [Int64]::MaxValue)
$f2 = [IO.File]::Open("$env:TEMP\t.lock", 'Open', 'Read', 'ReadWrite')   # opens fine
$f2.Read((New-Object byte[] 8), 0, 8)   # "The process cannot access the file because another process has locked a portio…

Following a standard InDesign table-of-contents tutorial (e.g. [Redokun: InDesign table of contents](https://www.redokun.com/blog/indesign-table-of-contents), [Webucator: How to Create a Table of Contents in Adobe InDesign](https://www.webucator.com/article/how-to-create-a-table-of-contents-in-adobe-indesig/)) in DesignCraft, the TOC dialog and `toc.generate` (since #850) cover the entry style, the page number position and the separator text. body:

## What's missing

title: [Feature] JPEG XL (.jxl) place and export
author: Gamedirection
body:
DesignCraft should place and export **JPEG XL** (`.jxl`) images, the same as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft. This is part of one request for the three apps: storytold/photocraft#6097.

Work that already exists in PhotoCraft:
- read: storytold/photocraft#2789, PR storytold/photocraft#2868 (`jxl-oxide`, a pure-Rust decoder);
- lossless write: PR storytold/photocraft#3387 (`zune-jpegxl`, a pure-Rust encoder);
- HDR export: storytold/photocraft#5569.

## What this solves in DesignCraft

- **Placed photos.** Photos are most of the content of magazines, books, catalogues and brochures, and more cameras, phones and apps now save `.jxl`. Today the user must convert each file in another app before placing it.
- **Smaller packages.** A layout with hundreds of placed images is often many GB. With JPEG XL, the linked JPEGs can be stored about 20% smaller with no change to a pixel, and the original JPEGs can be rebuilt bit for bit. Lossless images are smaller than PNG and TIFF. This saves disk space, upload time and transfer time to the printer or the client.
- **Print quality.** Print work needs high quality, 16-bit, wide gamut and CMYK-ready images. Lossy WebP cannot reach visually lossless quality (it always uses 4:2:0 chroma subsampling), and it is 8 bits only. JPEG XL keeps that quality at a smaller size than JPEG.
- **Page exports.** Exports of pages and spreads as images, at print resolution, often go past the WebP size limit of 16383 × 16383 pixels. JPEG XL has no practical limit.
- **PDF in the future.** The PDF Association selected JPEG XL as the preferred format for HDR images in PDF. When that is in the specification, DesignCraft can write JPEG XL images into PDF without conversion.

## What this solves

- **Smaller files with no loss.** An existing JPEG can be recompressed to JPEG XL about **20% smaller**, and the original JPEG can be rebuilt from it **bit for bit** ([jpegxl.info](https://jpegxl.info/old/why-jxl.html), [arXiv 2506.05987](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.0598…

title: IDML import: excessive spacing between consecutive paragraphs disrupts pagination
author: thisfilipe
body:
### Description When importing a long editorial IDML document created in Adobe InDesign, DesignCraft displays excessive vertical spacing between consecutive paragraphs that should appear much closer together. The original InDesign layout uses relatively tight spacing between verses, while DesignCraft introduces visibly larger gaps. These differences accumulate throughout the document, shifting text across frames and pages and significantly disrupting pagination. ### Reproduction evidence In `Stories/Story_ub3e.xml`, the passage following "Salmo 50" contains a `ParagraphStyleRange` using `ParagraphStyle/Normal`, with `SameParaStyleSpacing` explicitly set to zero: ```xml 0 segundo a tua benignidade;
apaga as minhas transgressões,
segundo a multidão das tuas misericórdias.
Lava-me completamente da minha iniquidade
e purifica-me do meu pecado.
``` **Clarification:** In IDML, `
` represents a paragraph break, even when multiple paragraphs are grouped within the same `ParagraphStyleRange`. A forced line break *within* a paragraph is represented differently (U+2028). Therefore, my original description incorrectly characterized these as forced line breaks within a single paragraph. The excessive spacing is observed between consecutive paragraphs, and the missing handling of `SameParaStyleSpacing` is a plausible explanation. ### Expected behavior Consecutive paragraphs respect the spacing rules recorded in the source IDML, including `SameParaStyleSpacing="0"`. Verses retain approximately the same vertical spacing as in InDesign, preserving text flow and pagination…

title: IDML import: placed images lose their InDesign FillColor recoloring
author: thisfilipe
body:
### Description
Placed decorative images import and render successfully once their external links are resolved, but DesignCraft does not reproduce the color treatment applied to them in InDesign.

The images are not missing. Their original tint/recoloring is missing.

### Reproduction evidence
The source IDML contains `<Image>` elements with their own `FillColor` attributes, including:

```xml
<Image FillColor="Color/C=0 M=100 Y=100 K=0" ...>
```

Examples include:
- `zigzag border 3.gif`
- `Header illumination - Gould.gif`

Other linked illustrations use `FillColor="Color/Black"`.

These settings are on the placed image elements, not merely on the surrounding page-item frames.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In InDesign, place a suitable monochrome/indexed decorative graphic and apply a color to the image.
2. Export the document as IDML.
3. Open it in DesignCraft with the image links correctly resolved.
4. Compare the resulting colors against InDesign.

### Expected behavior
Image recoloring specified by the IDML should be reproduced on screen and in exported output, where supported by the source image's color mode.

### Actual behavior
The image appears at the correct location, but without the applied color treatment.

### Environment
- DesignCraft v0.8.0 on Pop!_OS / GNOME
- Observed October 15, 2026
- Source IDML retains the color attributes

### Technical direction
The graphics import path in `crates/idml/src/import.rs` reads the linked image content, but the imported graphic representation does not appear to preserve these image-specific color attributes. Please verify the actual handling across import, canvas rendering and PDF export.

This issue is independent of broken absolute image paths.

title: IDML import: decorative paragraph borders render incorrectly and consecutive borders do not merge
author: thisfilipe
body: ### Description Paragraph border formatting imported from a complex InDesign layout does not match the original, in two ways: 1. Individual border boxes have the wrong appearance, including decorative corner geometry and potentially edge/offset behavior. 2. Borders that should continue or merge across consecutive paragraphs do not reproduce the original continuous box correctly. These are distinct visible problems, even if they share an implementation. ### Source IDML evidence The document's paragraph style `Normal - opcional` defines decorative borders, including: ```xml ParagraphBorderOn="true" ParagraphBorderTopLeftCornerOption="FancyCorner" ParagraphBorderTopRightCornerOption="FancyCorner" ParagraphBorderBottomLeftCornerOption="FancyCorner" ParagraphBorderBottomRightCornerOption="FancyCorner" ParagraphBorderTopLeftCornerRadius="7.086614173228347" ``` The IDML also contains `MergeConsecutiveParaBorders="true"` in its paragraph-style defaults and defines individual border widths and offsets. ### Expected behavior Border shape, decorative corners, edges, offsets and continuity match the InDesign layout. Consecutive paragraphs with compatible settings form a continuous border where required. ### Actual behavior The boxes do not match InDesign even individually, and continuity between consecutive boxes is also incorrect. ### Environment - DesignCraft v0.8.0 desktop on Linux (Pop!_OS / GNOME) - Observed October 15, 2026 - Real long-form editorial IDML ### Related work PR #360 ("Paragraph borders, shading, span space and list levels") appears to implement the relevant missing properties, including `MergeConsecutiveParaBorders`, corner shapes and border edges. This report documents a real-world failure that can serve as a regression test once that PR is merged. Paragraph spacing bugs can additionally affect box placement but do not fully explain the border-style differences.

title: Owner decision: run InDesign (ExtendScript) scripts? Proposal for a sandboxed script host
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
`docs/gaps.md` lists an ExtendScript/UXP-compatible DOM as an **owner decision** (150–250 h for a useful subset). Before anyone builds it, I'd like to ask whether you want it, and where it should live.

## Why
Template generators often deliver IDML with an InDesign script embedded in the document (as a document label). The user runs the script once to finish the layout. In our case it:
- sizes anchored images to the width of the column they end up in, keeping their proportions
- applies object styles from labels on each frame (`signet`, `level`, …)
- sets tables to the column width and applies table and paragraph styles
- asks one yes/no question

None of this can be done when the IDML is generated, because it depends on composition: which column an anchored image lands in. Today such files can't be finished in DesignCraft.

## What is already there
The engine groundwork is in five small PRs, useful on their own for agents and MCP:
- #1129 keyed script labels (insertLabel/extractLabel, IDML KeyValuePairs)
- #1130 `anchored.frame`: the frame and column an anchored object is set in (parentTextFrames)
- #1131 fixed column widths by command
- #1132 tables for scripts (list, width, paragraph style on cells)
- #1133 `object.graphic`: a placed graphic's kind, size and resolution

With these, every step of our script maps to existing commands. What's missing is something that runs the script.

## Proposal
A sandboxed ExtendScript host, built like pdfcraft-js, which runs Acrobat JavaScript in boa (a Rust JS engine; works on wasm):
- **Language and runtime:** ES3/ES5 JavaScript plus the ExtendScript extras scripts rely on: `$.writeln`, `UnitValue`, `#target`/`#include` ignored, `alert`/`confirm`/`prompt` through a UI callback (a fixed default when headless). No file, network or system access. Loops and recursion bounded.

title: [Feature Idea/Suggestion] Add support for Typst imports/placements
author: readtedium
body:
Beyond DesignCraft's goal to be a convention-friendly page design tool, one way that could make it stand out and perhaps offer new workflow advantages is through an integration with Typst.

[Typst](https://typst.app) is a modern, Rust-based typesetting system, akin to LaTeX but with more of an eye towards design. It is capable of compiling markup to a full page layout. It is not a full replacement for laying out images on a page or setting blending modes, but as it is a markup language, it could offer significant benefits from an automation standpoint. Its compiler is a set of Apache-2.0 crates that could be embedded directly. Many people already write technical and academic content in Typst. They may find it useful to integrate Typst content into a traditional page-layout editor for more visually-oriented designs.

### Proposal

`File > Place` (and `file.place` in `designcraft-cli` and the scripting API) accepts `.typ` files. The file is compiled with Typst, and the result is imported in one of the modes below.

**Phase 1:** frozen layout import

Typst compiles to a fully laid-out paged document: a tree of frames holding positioned text runs, shapes, paths, images and links, with exact coordinates. The importer walks that tree and creates native DesignCraft objects.

- One DesignCraft page per Typst page, at the same size.
- Text runs become positioned text frames with the right font, size and color, and shapes and images become native objects. Nothing is re-flowed, so the pages match Typst's output.
- Text is editable character by character but doesn't reflow.
- It works on any Typst document, including ones that use scripting, `#show` rules and packages, because it needs no semantic mapping.
- Unsupported constructs (some gradients, tiling patterns, blend modes) fall back to embedded SVG or raster, with a warning in the import options.

**Phase 2:** linked update

Placed Typst files are tracked as links. When the .typ source changes, the placed content can be upd…

title: Placing text into a primary text frame adds empty pages when page 1 holds little of it
author: noah1400
body:
With Smart Text Reflow on, placing a text file into the primary text frame can add many more pages than the text needs. The extra pages hold only empty threaded frames. They stay until the next edit of any kind, and a PDF exported before that has them as blank pages.

**Steps** (desktop app, main c2609f9):
1. File › New Document: Letter, one page, Primary Text Frame on.
2. Draw a graphic frame over the top of page 1 (x 36–576, y 36–600 pt) and give it Text Wrap › Wrap around bounding box. About ten lines of text fit below it.
3. Click into the primary text frame with the Type tool and File › Place a plain-text file of 16,520 characters (280 times `Words keep coming and the page fills up quickly with them. `).

**Actual:** 17 pages; pages 6–17 hold only empty frames. File › Export › PDF now writes 17 pages. The next edit, such as drawing a frame, takes the document to 5 pages.

**Expected:** 5 pages.

It happens whenever the first page holds little of the story. Turning Smart Text Reflow on with an overset story that starts with a 300 pt heading gives 56 pages for 5. Placing text that ends right at a page boundary leaves one empty page (250 times the line above: 4 pages for 3). Pasting the same text gives 5 pages: Edit › Paste runs `text.insert` inside it, so reflow runs twice and the second run removes the empty pages.

**Cause:** `autoflow()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/place_text.rs` estimates the frames still needed from how much the full frames hold, `want = (len - at).div_ceil(held / full)`, and adds that many pages at once. When the full frames hold less than a page usually does (text wrap, a large heading), the estimate is several times too high. Afterwards it removes only empty frames that share a page with the frame before them, so with Smart Text Reflow, one frame per page, every surplus page stays. Smart Text Reflow removes empty trailing pages only on the next command.

title: Feature request: frames whose content is rendered from source code (starting with LilyPond music notation)
author: laspapier
body:
Hi, and thanks for DesignCraft!

**Use case**
I would like to lay out pages that mix text and music scores (songbooks, teaching material, articles about music). Today I have to write the score in another tool, export it as an image, and place it in the document. When the score needs a change, I have to repeat the whole round trip.

**Proposed behavior**
A new kind of frame that holds source code and shows the rendered result:

1. At rest, the frame displays the rendered output (for example a music score).
2. On double-click (or click), the frame switches to edit mode and shows the LilyPond source, which I can edit as text.
3. When I confirm or click outside, the output is re-rendered and the frame updates.
4. The source is stored in the document, so reopening the file lets me keep editing it.
5. If the source does not compile, the frame keeps the last valid output and shows the error message instead of going blank.

**Possible implementation**
- Simplest: call an external `lilypond` binary with SVG output (cropped to the content), run it off the UI thread, and draw the resulting vector paths in the frame. This needs LilyPond installed, so it would be desktop-only and optional.
- Alternative: a different renderer such as Verovio, which can run in WebAssembly but takes MusicXML, MEI or ABC rather than LilyPond.
- Making the feature generic ("frame with source code and a pluggable renderer") could also cover other languages later, such as LaTeX math or Mermaid diagrams.

**Open questions**
- Would this fit the project's roadmap, or is there an existing extension mechanism I should use?
- How should such frames be handled in IDML, PowerPoint and PDF export? I would expect them to become vector paths or images there.

I am happy to test, and I can try to write a prototype if you can point me to the right place in the code (frame types, commands, UI). Thanks for considering it!

title: [SEVERE BUG] No way to leave presentation mode after it is toggled.
author: Sudo-DNF
body:
### Summary
After you switch to **View › Screen Mode › Presentation**, there is no way to leave it. Esc and the other usual shortcuts do nothing, and the menus are hidden, so you can't get back to Normal mode.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open any document (for example **Help › Sample Document**).
2. Choose **View › Screen Mode › Presentation**.
3. Try to leave presentation mode, for example by pressing Esc, Shift+W or W.

### Expected
As in InDesign, which DesignCraft follows for its shortcuts:
- **Esc** leaves presentation mode and goes back to the previous screen mode.
- **Shift+W** turns presentation mode on and off.
- There is also some way to leave with the mouse, for example a right-click menu or a visible exit control.

### Actual
The app stays in presentation mode. None of the keys above work, and the menu bar can't be reached. The only way out is to quit the app.

### Notes
- The built-in command list (`designcraft-cli commands`) and the documentation give no shortcut for presentation mode. The only screen-mode shortcut listed is **W** (`view.togglePreview`, Toggle Normal/Preview).
- `view.screenMode` takes `{mode: normal|preview|bleed|slug|presentation}`, but nothing in the user interface leads back to `normal` once presentation mode is on.
- If the last screen mode is saved and restored at launch (`UiState.screenMode`), the app might reopen in presentation mode. This hasn't been checked.

### Suggested fix
- Make Esc leave presentation mode.
- Bind Shift+W to turn presentation mode on and off, and show it in the Screen Mode menu.
- Optionally, show a brief "Press Esc to exit" hint when entering presentation mode.

### Environment
- DesignCraft 0.8.0 (`designcraft-0.8.0-1.x86_64`)
- Fedora 44, kernel 7.2.10-200.fc44.x86_64
- KDE Plasma on Wayland

title: [Report Issue & Feature Request] Thai text does not wrap correctly, request for Thai word segmentation support
author: liliaIsWriter-NotAProgrammer
body:
Hi! First of all, thank you for developing DesignCraft! I'm really excited about this project and would love to use it for Thai-language documents.(I'm a writer and this is very promising free tools to use to make e-book file.)

I've noticed that some Thai fonts already work in DesignCraft, which is great! However, there seems to be an issue with automatic line wrapping.

**The problem**
Unlike English, Thai generally doesn't use spaces to separate individual words. Instead, proper line wrapping requires the program to identify word boundaries automatically.

Currently, when I enter Thai text into a text frame, DesignCraft doesn't seem to recognize appropriate word boundaries, so the text doesn't wrap onto new lines correctly.

For example, this Thai text contains no spaces between words:

"ประเทศไทยมีสถานที่ท่องเที่ยวมากมายและมีอาหารอร่อยหลายอย่าง"

Ideally, DesignCraft should be able to wrap this text naturally according to the width of the text frame, without requiring users to manually insert spaces or line breaks.

**Possible solution**
I did a little research and found that there are already libraries that support Thai word segmentation and line breaking, including:

- [[ICU4X — icu_segmenter](https://docs.rs/icu_segmenter/latest/icu_segmenter/)](https://docs.rs/icu_segmenter/latest/icu_segmenter/), which supports dictionary-based line breaking for Thai and other languages.
- [[LibThai](https://github.com/tlwg/libthai)](https://github.com/tlwg/libthai), which provides Thai-specific word-breaking functionality.

Since DesignCraft is written in Rust, perhaps ICU4X could be a suitable option. However, I'm unsure. I have never used Rust before.

**Feature request**
If you have time in the future, I'd really appreciate it if you could consider adding automatic Thai word segmentation and line wrapping. This would make DesignCraft much more practical for creating Thai-language books and other publications.

Also, if there's already a setting, workaround, I'd be very …

title: Hyphenate Esperanto text
author: axel584
body:
Split out of #1142.

Text tagged Esperanto (Character › Language) isn't hyphenated: no hyphenation dictionary or patterns exist for `eo`, so a narrow justified column of Esperanto sets with wide gaps.

Esperanto is agglutinative, and its hyphenation convention breaks words between morphemes (prefixes, roots, suffixes), with the grammatical ending kept on the last piece. For example `tranĉ-ilo` (never `tran-ĉi-lo`), `mal-san-ul-ejo`, `vapor-ŝipo`. Syllable patterns trained from a word list would break inside roots, so a morpheme segmenter fits better.

Real-world case: Espéranto-France publications, where Esperanto words are tagged through a character style in French text (see #1142).

title: Spell-check Esperanto text
author: axel584
body:
Split out of #1142.

Text tagged Esperanto (Character › Language) isn't spell-checked: only English has a spelling dictionary. Esperanto words in a French or English document should be checked against an Esperanto word list, not flagged as English misspellings or skipped.

A suitable word list with a licence compatible with the repo still has to be found.

title: PDF/X-4 export: XMP metadata incomplete, Acrobat preflight fails
author: milanwulf
body:
**Type:** Bug

**Steps to reproduce:** Any document, `file.exportPdf {"standard":"x4"}`, then Acrobat Pro → Preflight → "Convert to PDF/X-4 (Coated FOGRA39)" (or "Verify compliance with PDF/X-4").

**Actual:** Preflight reports "PDF document is not compliant with PDF/X-4":

- `XMP does not have MetadataDate entry in the XMP Basic Schema` (`xmp:MetadataDate` missing)
- `XMP does not have a VersionID entry in the XMP Media Management Schema` (`xmpMM:VersionID` missing)

**Expected:** The exported file passes PDF/X-4 verification without post-processing. A PDF/X-4 from another tool (PDFlib) passes the same profile.

**Additional observations**

- `xmpMM:RenditionClass` is `proof`; `default` would be the usual value for print output.
- `/Title` and `dc:title` are `Untitled-2` for a saved document. The file name or a document title setting would be expected.

**Workaround:** Rewrite the XMP packet after export.
