title: Linked images are always stored inside the .designcraft file
author: milanwulf
body:
**Type:** Feature request

**Context:** We keep the layout in git and the images in an `assets/` folder. `links.list` shows the placed images as linked (`status: ok`, absolute path), but every image is also stored in the `.designcraft` zip (`assets/<id>.png`). A layout with one 10 MB photo is 10 MB, a thesis with 50 images several hundred MB, which makes versioning without Git LFS impractical.

**Request:** An option ("Store copies of linked images: off" or `file.save {"embedLinked":false}`) that saves only the links and reloads images from disk on open. Removing the asset copy from the zip by hand currently gives `status: modified` and the image is not drawn until `links.update`.

title: Text hyperlinks don't move when text is inserted or deleted before them
author: MKJJJ
body:
**Version:** DesignCraft 0.6.0 (desktop app + designcraft-cli 0.6.0), Windows 10 Pro

## What happens

A text hyperlink keeps its original byte offsets in the story when text is typed, pasted or deleted *before* it in the same story. The link source therefore no longer covers the linked words but whatever text now sits at those offsets. Character styles on the same text move correctly, so the underline (if it comes from a character style) still looks right while the clickable area in the exported PDF is wrong.

## Steps to reproduce

1. New document, create a text frame with the text: `Hello world. See page 2 for details.`
2. Select `page 2` and create a hyperlink (Type ▸ Hyperlinks & Cross-References ▸ New Hyperlink…, any destination).
3. Click at the very beginning of the text and type `ABC `.
4. In the Hyperlinks panel use “Go To Source” (or export a PDF and hover over the link).

**Expected:** the link source is still `page 2`.
**Actual:** the link source is `See pa`. It stays at the same offsets (bytes 17–23) and does not shift with the text.

Same result via scripting (`hyperlink.list` → `source.start/end`):

| Step | Story text | Link source |
|---|---|---|
| link created on “page 2” | `Hello world. See page 2 for details.` | `page 2` (bytes 17–23) |
| typed `ABC ` at the start | `ABC Hello world. See page 2 for details.` | `See pa` (bytes 17–23) |
| deleted it again (`story.replaceRange`) | `Hello world. See page 2 for details.` | `page 2` (bytes 17–23) |
| inserted `Größe ` (`story.replaceRange`) | `Größe Hello world. See page 2 for details.` | `ld. Se` (bytes 17–23) |

Inserting a single soft hyphen (U+00AD, 2 bytes) before a link is enough to shift it by 2 bytes. That makes this easy to hit in German texts, where discretionary hyphens are common.

## Expected behaviour

Like character-style runs (and like InDesign or Word), a text hyperlink source should be adjusted on every edit of its story:
- insert before the link → start and end shift by the inserted…

title: `story.replaceRange` accepts offsets inside a character, past the end, or with start > end, without an error
author: mischiatti75-spec
body:
**Summary.** `story.replaceRange` takes UTF-8 byte offsets (documented since #68, thanks). When the offsets are not valid for the story, it does not report an error: an offset inside a multi-byte character is moved silently, `end` past the end is clamped, and `start > end` past the end appends. The result looks like success, but the text is not what the agent meant.

**Environment.** designcraft-cli 0.9.0 (macOS universal, headless), macOS 26, Apple M4 Max.

**Steps to reproduce.** Base document, story `Città — perché è così` (27 bytes; `perché` is bytes 11–18):
```sh
B=(--cmd 'file.new={"preset":"A4"}' --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[50,50,400,200],"content":"text","text":"Città — perché è così"}')
for r in '{"start":11,"end":18,"text":"PERCHÉ"}' \
         '{"start":4,"end":5,"text":"a"}' \
         '{"start":8,"end":14,"text":"PERCHÉ"}' \
         '{"start":20,"end":999,"text":"!"}' \
         '{"start":30,"end":20,"text":"?"}'; do
  designcraft-cli run "${B[@]}" --cmd "story.replaceRange={\"story\":9,${r:1}" --cmd 'story.get={"story":9}' | tail -1
done
```

**Actual.** Every call returns `{"length": …}`, no error or warning:

| start..end | text | story after | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11..18 | `PERCHÉ` | `Città — PERCHÉ è così` | correct |
| 4..5 | `a` | `Cittaà — perché è così` | 4..5 is half of `à`: nothing replaced, `a` inserted |
| 8..14 | `PERCHÉ` | `Città cPERCHÉhé è così` | 8 is inside `—`: `— per` is gone and the `c` of `perché` ends up before the new text |
| 20..999 | `!` | `Città — perché !` | `end` clamped to 27 |
| 30..20 | `?` | `Città — perché è così?` | appended |

(8..14 is what an agent gets by counting characters for `perché`, so this is the easy mistake to make.)

**Expected.** Offsets that are not on a character boundary, greater than the story length, or with `start > end` are rejected with an error that gives the story length in bytes (and possibly the nearest valid boundaries). `text.select` could follow the same rule.

**Notes.** Optiona…

title: PDF export: no image downsampling, and `compressImages` leaves a large JPEG unchanged (1019 ppi in a 100 mm frame)
author: mischiatti75-spec
body:
**Summary.** Placed photos are embedded in the PDF at their original resolution. A 4000 × 3000 JPEG fitted into a 100 × 75 mm frame ends up at about 1019 ppi, and the PDF is as large as the photo. `compressImages: true` gives a byte-identical file, and I found no option to downsample to a target resolution. With a few photos per page a short photo report quickly reaches tens of MB.

**Environment.** designcraft-cli 0.9.0 (macOS universal, headless), macOS 26, Apple M4 Max.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```sh
python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.effect_noise((4000,3000),64).convert('RGB').save('big.jpg',quality=92)"   # ~9.5 MB
designcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.new={"preset":"A4"}' \
  --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[72,72,355,284],"content":"graphic"}' \
  --cmd 'file.place={"path":"big.jpg","frame":8}' \
  --cmd 'object.fit={"mode":"fitProportionally"}' \
  --cmd 'file.exportPdf={"path":"out.pdf","compressImages":true}' \
  --cmd 'preflight.run={"minPpi":150}'
pdfimages -list out.pdf
```

**Actual.** `out.pdf` is 9,504,540 bytes, the same with or without `compressImages`. `pdfimages -list`: one JPEG, 4000 × 3000, x-ppi/y-ppi 1019. Preflight reports 0 errors and 0 warnings.

**Expected.** An export option to downsample images above a threshold to a target resolution (as in the usual PDF presets, e.g. "bicubic downsample to 150/300 ppi for images above 225/450 ppi"), with JPEG quality. If `compressImages` is not meant to do this, a line in its description saying what it does.

**Why / use case.** Photo reports and leaflets sent by e-mail or uploaded to portals with size limits. Today the PDF has to go through Ghostscript afterwards: on a photo report from an earlier test that took it from 5.1 MB to 0.7 MB at 200 ppi, with text and fonts unchanged.

**Notes.** A `maxPpi` check in `preflight.run` (warn above N effective ppi) would also help an agent notice the problem before exporting.

title: feat(cli): `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` for `designcraft-cli mcp`
author: S3Serv
body:
`designcraft-cli mcp` has no way to confine which files the agent's commands may read and write.
PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already solve this with `--automation-read-root <dir>` /
`--automation-write-root <dir>`, where omitting a root deliberately denies that direction of
access. This asks for the same two flags here, with the same semantics.

### Why

The README invites agent use ("let an agent drive it over MCP"), but without roots the MCP server
runs with the full permissions of the user who launched it. An agent driving it can read and write
anything that user can — SSH keys, `.env` files, password-manager exports, cloud-synced
directories. That is a lot of trust to extend to a tool whose job is to open and save files, and it
is the one thing standing between `designcraft-cli mcp` and an unattended agent workflow.

PhotoCraft's enforcement is exactly the right shape in practice: a save outside the root returns

    automation path rejected: absolute paths must be inside the automation root: `/path/outside`

...and nothing is written. Having the same guarantee in `designcraft-cli` would make the five CLIs
consistent and let the same agent configuration work across the suite.

### Current workaround, and why it is not sufficient

On macOS I wrap the server in the kernel sandbox:

    /usr/bin/sandbox-exec -D ROOT=/path/to/project -f craft.sb designcraft-cli mcp

This works, and it actually catches a little more than a path check would — it blocked a temp file
written to `$HOME` during a save (`~/.designcraft-save-*.tmp`) that an in-app check on the target
path would have missed. But:

- `sandbox-exec` is formally deprecated by Apple.
- It is macOS-only. There is no equivalent for Linux or Windows users, so on those platforms there
  is no way to confine `designcraft-cli mcp` at all.
- It is per-user configuration rather than something the tool guarantees, so a careless launch
  silently has no boundary.

title: feat(desktop): `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` for `DesignCraft --control`
author: S3Serv
body:
`DesignCraft --control 7981` has no way to confine what the control channel may read and write.
PhotoCraft and VectorCraft take `--automation-read-root <dir>` / `--automation-write-root <dir>` on
the **desktop app**, not only on the CLI, and enforce them on control requests. This asks for the
same two flags on `DesignCraft`, with the same semantics.

### Why it has to be on the app, not the CLI

`designcraft-cli mcp --connect` only relays: the app process does the actual opening and saving. So any
boundary passed to the CLI is irrelevant in that mode, and the app's own roots are the only thing
that can confine an attached agent.

On macOS I confine the *headless* path with the kernel sandbox (`/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`), but that
cannot help here — the app is launched from the Dock, outside the sandbox, and is the process doing
the I/O. The result is that an agent attached to a live DesignCraft window can read and write anything the
user can, with no way to narrow it. VectorCraft documents exactly this split and solves it:

    vectorcraft --control 7979 --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

and a save outside the write root comes back as an ordinary error reply instead of being written —
which I verified on 0.12.0.

### Request

`--automation-read-root <dir>` and `--automation-write-root <dir>` on `DesignCraft`, honoured for every
control request, with a root left out granting none of that access. Environment-variable
equivalents (as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft have) would be welcome but are secondary.

This is the desktop-app counterpart of the CLI request; filing it separately so the two can be
tracked on their own.

Happy to test a build.

Environment: macOS 27.0 (arm64), DesignCraft 0.8.0

title: Web build: a host bridge for embedding pages (?host=parent), like PdfCraft's
author: philkunz
body:
We run the DesignCraft web build as a window in a web desktop that frames the web build, the same way as PdfCraft, GridCraft and CADCraft. Their `?host=parent` bridge lets the embedding page open files and receive saves. Without one, DesignCraft can't tell the page about unsaved changes, so the page can't ask before a window with edits closes, and saves become browser downloads.

Proposal, the same family protocol as storytold/deckcraft#983 and storytold/wordcraft#2919, posted to the parent only with `?host=parent`:
- `designcrafteady` / `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-philkunz-foss-global/410470bf-81b1-4e09-9a60-86819268a2c6/scratchpad/issues/designcraftiled`: start-up handshake
- `designcraft:open {name, bytes}`: the parent hands over a file to open
- `designcraftve, Save As and exports go to the parent instead of a download
- `designcraft:dirty {dirty}`: on every change of the unsaved state

title: Standardise macOS keyboard shortcuts across the Craft suite
author: andeecollard
body:
## Proposal

Make macOS keyboard and menu conventions consistent across the Craft suite. This issue is a cross-repository coordination proposal; each affected app will need its own implementation PR. Please move the shared standard to the appropriate suite-wide repository if one is available.

On macOS, platform conventions should be the default. Creative-app compatibility mappings can be offered as an explicit optional preset, with conflicts clearly explained.

## Proposed macOS defaults

| Action | Shortcut / behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Settings… | ⌘,; visible in the application menu |
| Hide application | ⌘H |
| Hide other applications | ⌥⌘H |
| Minimize window | ⌘M |
| Close document/window | ⌘W; prompt appropriately for unsaved work |
| Quit | ⌘Q; handle unsaved work safely |
| New / Open / Save | ⌘N / ⌘O / ⌘S where applicable |
| Undo / Redo | ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z |
| Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All | ⌘X / ⌘C / ⌘V / ⌘A; act on the focused editor |
| Find | ⌘F where applicable |
| Full screen | ⌃⌘F where supported |

## Conflicts identified in a local source review

- DesignCraft and VectorCraft declare Preferences as `Cmd+K`. VectorCraft also accepts `Cmd+,` separately, leaving its displayed/default binding inconsistent.
- VectorCraft assigns `Cmd+H` to Hide Edges, moves Hide Application to `Ctrl+Cmd+H`, and moves Minimize to `Ctrl+Cmd+M`.
- DesignCraft assigns `Cmd+H` to frame edges while installing the native Hide menu item, creating competing definitions. Its native application menu does not include Settings.
- PhotoCraft assigns `Cmd+H` to Extras and `Cmd+M` to Curves.
- FilmCraft assigns `Cmd+M` to Export.
- LightCraft already declares `Cmd+,` for Settings and explicitly yields standard editing shortcuts to focused text inputs; this is useful behaviour to retain across the suite.

These are source findings, not a completed runtime audit of every app. Other apps and the launcher should be checked against the same standard.

## Suggested rollout and acceptance criteria…

title: Math: matrix environments (pmatrix, bmatrix, vmatrix, …) are not supported
author: okc0mputex
body:
**Type:** feature gap · **Area:** `crates/engine/src/math.rs` (`math.insert`, `math.svg`)

Split out of #1321.

## Minimal repro

```
file.new {"width": 470, "height": 60, "pages": 1, "margins": 0}
math.insert {"latex": "A = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\\\ 3 & 4 \\end{pmatrix}, \\quad \\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\\\ c & d \\end{vmatrix} = ad - bc", "size": 15, "x": 10, "y": 10}
```

Run with `designcraft-cli script repro.dcs --export out.png`.

## Actual (main, 443ea46)

`\begin{pmatrix}…\end{pmatrix}` comes out as raw source (`\beginpmatrix1&2\\3&4\endpmatrix`), and so does every other matrix environment.

![main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okc0mputex/designcraft/pr-assets/matrix_main.png)

With the environments PR (#1325), the matrices become grids but have no delimiters:

![with the environments PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okc0mputex/designcraft/pr-assets/matrix_with_grids.png)

## Expected

`pmatrix`, `bmatrix`, `Bmatrix`, `vmatrix`, `Vmatrix`, `matrix` and `smallmatrix` set as a centred grid with the matching delimiters: `( )`, `[ ]`, `{ }`, `| |`, `‖ ‖`, and none for `matrix`/`smallmatrix` (`smallmatrix` at script size). The delimiters are sized to the grid, the way `\left…\right` already sizes them.

## Suggested approach

Reuse the grid from #1325, with centred columns, wrapped in the existing `Node::Fenced` delimiter sizing. Keep the `MAX_NESTING` checks (#954).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each of the seven environments parses to a grid with its delimiter pair (none for `matrix`/`smallmatrix`), and no raw `\begin`, `&` or `\\` reaches the output.
- The delimiters span the grid's full height; a 3-row matrix is taller than a 2-row one.
- Columns are centred; `&` and `\\` inside braces or a nested environment don't split cells.
- Unclosed or deeply nested matrices don't panic and stay within the nesting cap.

## Related

#1325 (environments as grids), #1038 (`\left…\right`), #954 / #712 / #920 (nesting cap).

![main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okc0mputex/designcraft/pr-assets/accents_main.png)

## Expected

`\vec`, `\hat`, `\bar`/`\overline`, `\dot`, `\ddot`, `\tilde`, `\widehat` and `\widetilde` put the accent centred over the base, raised by the base's height. A wide accent (`\widehat`, `\widetilde`, `\overline`) stretches over the whole argument.

## Suggested approach

Add a `Node::Accent(char, Box<Node>, wide: bool)`. Lay out the base, then place the spacing-accent glyph or a drawn stroke (an arrow for `\vec`, a rule for `\bar`/`\overline`) centred above it at `base.asc + gap`. The bundled fonts have the spacing accents ˆ ˜ ¯ ˙ ¨ and the arrow →. Keep the `MAX_NESTING` checks (#954).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each accent command parses to an accent over its argument; no raw `\vec` etc. reaches the output.
- The accent is centred over the base and sits above its ascent: `\hat{x}` is taller than `x`, and `\hat{A}` sits higher than `\hat{a}`.
- `\overline{AB}` and `\widehat{xyz}` span the argument's width.
- Nested accents (`\hat{\bar{x}}`) work and stay within the nesting cap.

## Related

#954 / #712 / #920 (nesting cap), #1038.

title: Equations: keep the LaTeX source in IDML export and re-import it as an editable equation
author: okc0mputex
body:
**Type:** feature request · **Area:** `crates/idml`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/mathexpr.rs`

Split out of #1323.

## Background

Today (main, 443ea46), checked with a synthetic document holding one `math.insert {"latex": "\\frac{a}{b}"}`: an equation is a graphic frame named `Math` holding the typeset SVG, with its LaTeX source in the item's alt text so it can be edited. There is no MathML support anywhere in the codebase (`rg -i mathml` finds nothing).

**IDML export** writes the frame as a `<Rectangle Name="Math">` with an embedded `<Image>` (`LinkResourceURI="file:math.svg"`). The LaTeX source is not written anywhere in the package (no alt text, no label, no XML), so opening the exported IDML again gives a plain picture that can no longer be edited as math. (Side observation: the link declares `LinkResourceFormat="$ID/Portable Network Graphics (PNG)"` for SVG data.)

## Request

- On export, write the LaTeX as the frame's custom alt text, so the IDML also stays accessible:
  ```xml
  <ObjectExportOption AltTextSourceType="SourceCustom" CustomAltText="\frac{a}{b}"/>
  ```
- Optionally also write it as a key/value label (`<KeyValuePair Key="designcraft:latex" …/>`, cf. #1129).
- On import, a `Math` frame with that label (or that alt text) becomes an editable equation again.

## Acceptance criteria

- Export → import keeps `alt_text` and editability (`math.insert {id, latex}` works on the re-imported item) for both frame and inline equations.
- The re-imported equation renders the same as before the round trip.
- A `Math`-named frame without LaTeX alt text or label imports as a plain graphic, as today.
- The SVG link declares an SVG format rather than PNG.

## Related

#1129 (keyed labels / IDML KeyValuePairs), #1215 (editing equations in place), #920 (IDML resource limits), #1181.

title: Equations: turn LaTeX in text (delimiters or a character style) into inline equations on import
author: okc0mputex
body:
**Type:** feature request · **Area:** text/IDML import, `crates/engine/src/cmd/mathexpr.rs`

Split out of #1323.

## Background

Today (main, 443ea46), checked with a synthetic document holding one `math.insert {"latex": "\\frac{a}{b}"}`: an equation is a graphic frame named `Math` holding the typeset SVG, with its LaTeX source in the item's alt text so it can be edited. There is no MathML support anywhere in the codebase (`rg -i mathml` finds nothing).

LaTeX that arrives as text in a story (a common way manuscripts carry equations) stays plain text: there is no way to turn it into equations other than scripting `math.insert` for each one.

## Request

An opt-in import rule that turns a story range into an inline equation. The range is marked either:

- by delimiters: `$…$` or `\(…\)` (display: `$$…$$` or `\[…\]`, if wanted); or
- by a chosen character style (for example a style named "LaTeX").

Example (plain text in a story):

```
The ratio $\frac{a}{b}$ is positive.
```

Expected with the rule on: "The ratio ", an inline equation `\frac{a}{b}`, " is positive.". With the rule off: unchanged text, as today.

## Acceptance criteria

- Off by default; existing imports are unchanged.
- With the delimiter rule on, each delimited range becomes one inline `Math` item with that LaTeX; escaped `\$` and unmatched delimiters stay as text.
- With the character-style rule on, each run in that style becomes an equation and the style is not applied to the result.
- An expression the typesetter can't parse is left as text with a warning, never a panic.

## Related

#1140 (Typst imports), #1181 (source-rendered frames), #1215.

title: Frame edges cost ~200 ms per frame on large documents; start-up GPU fallback blames the backend when the app freezes
author: AndreRese
body:
Two findings from debugging one large document in **0.9.0** (Windows 11 x64 MSI; Ryzen 7 5800X, Radeon RX 7600 XT, 1920×1080 @ 120 Hz). They're independent, so I'm happy to split them into two issues.

The document is an IDML from InDesign: 95 pages, 48 spreads, ~6,870 page items (2,775 text frames, 1,770 groups, 1,765 ovals, 462 rectangles), 2,832 stories. Preflight reports **2,324 overset frames**, mostly small numbered callouts that overflow by 1–2 characters (two of the document's fonts are missing on this machine). Its cross-story list is turned off, so #508 doesn't apply.

## 1. Frame edges: ~200 ms of UI work per frame

With frame edges on, the app runs at about 4.5 fps whatever you do: hovering, changing pages, zooming. Hiding them (**View › Show/Hide Frame Edges**) brings it to 60–80 fps. Measured over the control channel: `perf.frameMs` (time spent in `DesignApp::ui`) while sending `ui.move` / `ui.set` requests, window 1440×900, fit-spread zoom:

| | OpenGL | DirectX 12 |
|---|---|---|
| Frame edges **on**: UI work per frame | 198 ms (4.8 fps) | 202 ms (4.4 fps) |
| Frame edges **off**: UI work per frame | 0.9 ms (~80 fps) | 3.1 ms (~78 fps) |
| Canvas render (`renderMs`, worker thread) | 18–25 ms | 18 ms |

The graphics backend makes no difference. Closing the Links panel doesn't either (198 ms).

**Where the time goes.** I took 60 stack samples of the UI thread; the release build has no PDB, so frames were named from `.pdata` plus the source locations and literals each function references. In 57/60 samples the thread is inside the canvas, and in **44/60 it is in `find_in`**, the recursive search behind `Document::find`. It gets there two ways:

- **27/60: [`overset_frames`](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/7cb8b12507def48fb9346e5004340b5e8e4cfcb7/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L1301-L1320) → `Cache::get`, 19 of them in [`signature()`](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/7cb8b12507def48fb9346e5004340b5e8e4cfcb7/crates/compose/src/cach…

title: Web build: report the open document in the viewport title
author: robertcsakany
body:
The web build sends no `ViewportCommand::Title` naming the open document (eframe would log it as `Unhandled egui viewport command: Title(…)` on the web). WordCraft, GridCraft, PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do (`<document>[ •] — <App>`).

An embedding host (pi-agent-dashboard runs the web build in a sandboxed iframe and delivers the document as a synthetic drop) uses that title to confirm WHICH document the app opened and whether it has unsaved changes. Without it the host can only assume the drop worked after a delay; when a drop is refused, the app's default document is mistaken for the file (seen with CADCraft 0.8.0 and a `.dwg`: it showed `Drawing1`).

Ask: send `Title("<file name>[ •] — <App>")` on open, rename and dirty change, like WordCraft.

title: Proposal: Japanese units (Q, H, mm) and multilingual measurement input, in small PRs
author: con3code
body:
Japanese layout is specified in its own units. Type size is in **Q** (級, 0.25 mm), line feed in **H** (歯, also 0.25 mm), and pages in millimetres. A Japanese spec sheet reads "body 13Q, 22H, 40 characters × 16 lines". Korean work uses the same 0.25 mm unit as 급 (gp) next to points and millimetres. Chinese work uses millimetres and points. All three count indents and spacing in characters: em (全角, 전각) and en (半角, 반각).

DesignCraft already has Q and Ha in `geom::units`. What's missing is mostly wiring. I'd like to propose small PRs, each following what InDesign's Japanese edition does (observed below) or a published requirement, and to ask four decisions up front.

## What upstream has already settled

- **#1074:** the ruler menus list the units of InDesign's English menus, without Q and Ha (a document already in Q or Ha keeps its unit there). The Japanese edition differs, as observed below. This proposal adds its units only with Show CJK Features, so the English menus stay as #1074 left them.
- **#325 / #549 / #923:** units are chosen in New Document, Preferences › Units & Increments and the ruler menus.
- **#1272, #1290, #1196:** a field reads a bare number in its own units, preset captions follow the selected units, and tool readouts use the document's units. The fixes below follow the same pattern.
- **#1073:** formatting follows InDesign's fields (decimals per unit).
- **#1259 (open):** asks for a Japanese business card, 91 × 55 mm.
- **#1200 (open):** a font size change in the top bar hides the text. That is a rendering problem; nothing here touches it, and the field change below keeps the same commit path.

## What InDesign's Japanese edition does (observed, InDesign 2025)

Black-box observation with a new synthetic document, as `CLAUDE.md` allows. Nothing from InDesign is committed or copied: feature names and behaviour only.

**Units & Increments offers:**

| Setting | Units offered |
|---|---|
| Rulers | points, picas, inches, decimal inches, millimetres, ce…

title: Type fields drop the unit typed: `13Q` sets 13 pt
author: con3code
body:
Part of #1357.

About 30 fields that hold a length in points (character size, leading and baseline shift, stroke weights, underline and strikethrough, paragraph rules and borders, ruby, tate-chu-yoko and kenten, drop shadow) are plain number fields with a ` pt` suffix (`NumField::number(.., " pt", ..)`). Their parser keeps only digits and operators, so `13Q` sets 13 pt and `5mm` sets 5 pt, with no error.

InDesign converts what is typed: in a field shown in Q, `12pt` becomes 16.933 Q (observed in InDesign 2025, Japanese edition).

**Steps.** Select text, type `13Q` into the Character panel's size field, press Return.
**Expected.** 9.213 pt (13 × 0.25 mm). **Actual.** 13 pt.

A fix is ready as a PR.

Generated with Claude Code

title: IDML writes Q ruler units as `U`; InDesign writes `Q`
author: con3code
body:
Part of #1357.

`idml::names::unit_out` maps `Unit::Q` to `"U"`, and `unit_in` maps nothing to Q. InDesign writes Q as `Q`: an IDML saved from InDesign 2025 (Japanese edition) with text size in Q has `TextSizeMeasurementUnits="Q"` on `ViewPreference`. `U` is a different unit; the scripting reference lists `Q`, `HA`, `U` and `BAI` as separate `MeasurementUnits`.

So a document with Q rulers goes out as `U`, and an InDesign file with Q rulers comes back in points. Units DesignCraft doesn't have (`U`, `Bai`, `Mils`, `AmericanPoints`) also become points without a word in the import report.

A fix is ready as a PR.

Generated with Claude Code

title: Japanese page presets: JIS B4, B5, B6 and a 91 × 55 mm business card
author: con3code
body:
Part of #1357; see also #1259.

- `B5` in New Document is ISO B5 (176 × 250 mm). In Japan B5 means JIS B5 (182 × 257 mm), and InDesign's Japanese edition offers B5 at 182 × 257 mm.
- There is no Japanese business card; #1259 asks for 91 × 55 mm.

Proposal:
- add JIS B4, B5 and B6 (257 × 364, 182 × 257, 128 × 182 mm, from JIS P 0138);
- add a business card of 91 × 55 mm.

The sizes come from the standard and #1259, not from InDesign's preset list.

**Decision needed:** should `B5` be split into `B5 (ISO)` and `B5 (JIS)`, or should the list follow the interface language (JIS B5 in Japanese)?

Generated with Claude Code

title: Text size, typographic and stroke unit settings (and their IDML attributes)
author: con3code
body:
Part of #1357.

DesignCraft has ruler units only, so type fields can't show Q (級) or H (歯), and IDML drops these attributes on `ViewPreference`: `TextSizeMeasurementUnits`, `TypographicMeasurementUnits` and `StrokeMeasurementUnits`.

InDesign 2025's Japanese edition offers these in Units & Increments (observed):

| Setting | Units offered |
|---|---|
| Text size | points, Q, American points |
| Composition (typographic) | points, H, U, Bai, mils, American points |
| Stroke | points, millimetres |
| Rulers | as in English, plus H, American points, U, Bai, mils (no Q) |

Proposal:
- three per-document settings, kept through IDML:
  - Text Size: points or Q;
  - Typographic: points or Ha;
  - Stroke: points or millimetres.
- Q and Ha show only with Show CJK Features (`docs/cjk.md`, Decision 1), or while the document uses them.
- With Show CJK Features, the rulers also offer Ha, as the Japanese edition does. The English menus stay as #1074 left them.
- Fields show their setting's unit and step by one of it.
- Frame grids (#428) follow the text size and typographic units.

Builds on #1359.

Generated with Claude Code

title: Unit names aren't translated
author: con3code
body:
Part of #1357.

The unit names in Preferences › Units & Increments, the ruler menus and New Document have no rows in the i18n tables, so they show in English in every interface language: Points, Picas, Inches, Inches Decimal, Millimeters, Centimeters, Ciceros, Agates, Pixels, Q, Ha.

Proposal: add them to every table. For example:
- Japanese: ポイント, パイカ, インチ, ミリメートル, 級, 歯;
- Korean: 급 for Q;
- Chinese: 毫米 for millimetres.

The suffixes in fields (`pt`, `mm`, `Q`, `H`) stay ASCII in every language, as InDesign's do, so a copied value pastes back anywhere.

Generated with Claude Code

title: Measurement input: full-width digits, unit words and a decimal comma
author: con3code
body:
Part of #1357.

`parse_measure` reads ASCII only, so fields reject:
- full-width input, which Japanese and Chinese input methods often type (`１３Ｑ`, `１２ｍｍ`);
- unit words (`13級`, `22歯`, `5ミリ`, `5毫米`, `12포인트`);
- a decimal comma (`12,5 mm`), used in most European languages.

InDesign rejects these too, so this would be an improvement beyond parity, not a parity fix.

Proposal: in `parse_measure`, so every field gets it:
- read full-width ASCII (U+FF01–FF5E) and U+3000 as ASCII;
- accept a short table of unit words:
  - Q: `級`, `급`, `gp` (KLREQ 7.4.1)
  - H: `歯`
  - mm: `ミリ`, `㎜`, `毫米`, `밀리미터`
  - cm: `センチ`, `厘米`, `센티미터`
  - pt: `ポイント`, `磅`, `点`, `포인트`
  - in: `インチ`, `英寸`, `인치`, `˝`
  - pica: `pi`
- read a comma between digits as a decimal point when there is no dot.

**Decision needed:** is this welcome beyond InDesign? Should the decimal comma be read for everyone, or only in languages that use one?

Generated with Claude Code

title: em and en in measurement fields
author: con3code
body:
Part of #1357.

CJK layout counts indents and spacing in characters, and Latin layout uses em and en too:
- **JLREQ** takes a one-em first-line indent as the usual case (3.1.5) and indents headings by characters of the base size (2.2.5);
- **CLREQ** treats fullwidth and halfwidth as measures of character width (note in 4.1);
- **KLREQ** counts indentation in the paragraph's character width (7.2.3.1).

No field accepts `1em` or `0.5en`, so a one-character indent has to be worked out in points and redone when the size changes.

Proposal:
- `1em` is the type size of the text the field applies to, and `1en` is half of it. The base is passed the way `%` gets its base (`parse_measure_rel`):
  - indent, spacing, tab and offset fields use the selected text's or style's size;
  - frame fields use the size of the frame's first paragraph;
  - fields without text reject em and en.
- Words: `全角`, `字`, `전각`, `글자` for em; `半角`, `반각` for en. `ch` is left out, since CSS uses it for the width of a zero.
- The value is converted to points on entry, so the model and IDML don't change.

title: Direct Selection: double-clicking a text frame should switch to Type tool
author: el-j
body:
### Summary

In InDesign (and VectorCraft #1973), double-clicking a text frame with the Direct Selection tool (`A`) immediately switches to the Type tool and positions the text insertion caret at the clicked character for inline editing. This applies to both standalone text frames and leaf text frames nested inside groups.

### Current Behavior

Double-clicking a text frame with the Direct Selection tool only inspects for corner widgets and does not switch to the Type tool. The user has to manually select the Type tool (`T`) before they can edit text in the frame.

### Expected Behavior

Double-clicking a text frame with the Direct Selection tool switches to the Type tool and places the caret at the clicked character (preserving lock protection on locked frames, layers, or groups).

title: Selection tool: double-clicking a group should drill down into nested items
author: el-j
body:
### Summary

In InDesign, double-clicking a group with the Selection tool (`V`) drills down into the group hierarchy one level per double-click along the ancestry chain, selecting the child item or subgroup under the pointer.

### Current Behavior

Double-clicking a group with the Selection tool does not drill down into child items; it keeps the top-level group selected.

### Expected Behavior

Double-clicking a group with the Selection tool drills down one level per double-click into the clicked child item or subgroup along the ancestry chain.

title: Type tool: Escape should return to the selection tool used before double-clicking
author: el-j
body:
### Summary

When entering text editing via double-clicking with a selection tool (such as the Direct Selection tool `A` or Selection tool `V`), pressing Escape should exit text editing and return back to the tool that was used before double-clicking into text (parity with VectorCraft #1974).

### Current Behavior

`TypeTool` on Escape currently hardcodes switching to `"selection"` (`Action::SwitchTool("selection".into())`), so if the user double-clicked into text from the Direct Selection tool, Escape switches them to the standard Selection tool instead.

### Expected Behavior

Pressing Escape while in the Type tool restores the tool used prior to entering text editing (`directSelection` or `selection`) and keeps the text frame selected.

title: Selection tool: Escape should climb to parent group hierarchy
author: el-j
body:
### Summary

In InDesign, when an item or subgroup nested inside a group is selected with the Selection tool, pressing Escape moves the selection one level up to the enclosing parent group.

### Current Behavior

Pressing Escape when a child item inside a group is selected deselects everything immediately rather than climbing back up to the enclosing group.

### Expected Behavior

• When a nested item or subgroup is selected with the Selection tool, pressing Escape selects its immediate parent group.
• Repeated Escape presses climb up the group ancestry chain until reaching the top-level group, where a final Escape deselects.

title: Direct Selection tool: single-click should select child items directly in groups and nested groups
author: el-j
body:
### Summary

In InDesign, clicking with the Direct Selection tool (`A`) directly selects individual child items inside groups and nested groups, without ungrouping or affecting sibling items.

### Current Behavior

Single-clicking on a child item inside a group with the Direct Selection tool does not select the leaf item directly.

### Expected Behavior

Single-clicking with the Direct Selection tool on a child item inside a group or nested group directly selects that leaf item.

title: Type tool: enable direct text editing and caret placement in text frames nested in groups
author: el-j
body:
### Summary

In InDesign, selecting the Type tool (`T`) and clicking directly into a text frame that is nested inside a group or nested groups immediately places the insertion caret and allows inline text editing, text selection, and typography changes.

### Current Behavior

Clicking with the Type tool on a text frame nested inside a group does not hit-test through the group to the text frame, preventing direct caret placement and inline text editing.

### Expected Behavior

• Clicking with the Type tool directly on a text frame nested inside a group hit-tests the leaf text frame and places the insertion caret at the click point.
• Multi-click selection (double/triple/quad-click) and drag-selection work directly on grouped text frames.
• Locked text frames, frames in locked groups, or frames on locked layers do not accept caret placement.

title: Direct Selection tool: marquee should select child items directly in groups and nested groups
author: el-j
body:
### Summary

In InDesign, dragging a marquee with the Direct Selection tool (`A`) selects individual child items inside groups and nested groups intersecting the marquee bounds, without selecting whole groups or requiring ungrouping.

### Current Behavior

Dragging a marquee with the Direct Selection tool does not select individual child items inside groups intersecting the marquee.

### Expected Behavior

Dragging a marquee with the Direct Selection tool selects all unlocked, visible child items within the marquee bounds across nested groups.

title: Links panel blocks the UI while polling linked files every 500 ms
author: AndreRese
body:
## Summary

Opening the Links panel on a link-heavy IDML causes repeated UI stalls. The panel runs `links.list` synchronously during the egui UI pass, and repeats it every 500 ms. That command checks linked paths on disk and can read complete linked assets for comparison.

With missing local/mapped paths this produces recurring hitches. With a slow or disconnected mapped/network drive, the operating-system filesystem call can block much longer and make the entire application appear frozen or Not Responding.

This is separate from whether a network path is accepted by the stored-path security policy. The problem is that allowed filesystem checks run synchronously on the UI thread.

## Environment

- DesignCraft 0.10.0
- Commit: `8dff7ecd`
- Windows, release build
- Real-world IDML: approximately 6.25 MB
- 572 link occurrences in the package
- 379 rows returned by `links.list`
- 228 rows use UNC-style paths such as `//server/share/...`
- 151 rows use a mapped drive such as `K:/...`
- All 379 links were missing in the test environment

The IDML itself is proprietary, so it is not attached.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an IDML or DesignCraft document containing hundreds of linked graphics.
2. Include links on a missing or slow mapped drive for the worst case.
3. Choose **Window › Links**.
4. Try to interact with the window while the Links panel remains open.

## Actual result

The UI pauses while the link list is produced, then repeats the work while the panel remains open. Slow filesystem paths can freeze the whole application rather than only leaving the affected link in a pending or missing state.

The panel also lays out every row in one non-virtualized grid, which adds work for large lists.

## Expected result

The Links panel should display cached or “checking” statuses immediately and remain responsive while file status is checked in the background. A slow, unavailable, or disconnected linked location must not block the UI event loop.

I compa…

title: [Feature Request] Book management system (.dcbook / .indb equivalent) for modular projects
author: joaovictorximenes0-eng
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
When laying out long-form publications (novels, anthologies, manuals), keeping the entire project in a single document can impact performance and stability. 

Currently, splitting a project into modular chapter files requires layout artists to:
1. Manually calculate and override starting page numbers for every chapter file.
2. Manually re-export individual PDFs whenever a page count changes.
3. Use external CLI/GUI utilities (`pdfunite`, `PDFsam`) to merge the final output.

### Describe the solution you'd like
A dedicated **Book Panel** (and associated `.dcbook` project file format) to streamline multi-file publications:

- **Document List Management:** Ability to add, remove, and reorder `.designcraft` files (chapters, interludes, front/back matter).
- **Dynamic Page Renumbering:** Automatic sequential page numbering across all chained documents in the book panel.
- **Style Synchronization:** Designate a "Style Source" document to push Paragraph/Character styles, Swatches, and Master Pages to all other files.
- **Unified PDF Export:** A single action to export all chained documents into a single consolidated PDF.

### Context & Impact
This is a core workflow feature for long-form editorial design (equivalent to InDesign's `.indb` Book feature). Adding this would make DesignCraft a fully viable open-source alternative for book designers and independent publishers.

title: Optical kerning sets body text about 1.8% tighter than InDesign, so imported books reflow (follow-up to #181 / #427)
author: director-LAC
body:
Version: designcraft-cli 0.10.0, main 8dff7ec, Linux x86_64. Reference: the InDesign 21.6 PDF of the same IDML.

Text: Source Serif 4 Regular 9.5/14.5 pt. DesignCraft uses its bundled 4.005, whose glyph advances match the copy InDesign embedded. Left justified, `KerningMethod="$ID/Optical"`, tracking 0, word spacing 80/100/133, letter spacing 0/0/0, glyph scaling 100/100/100, Adobe Paragraph Composer, no local overrides. So kerning is the only thing changing letter widths in InDesign.

Method: for each body line, the sum of its word widths (`pdftotext -bbox`) divided by the same words' unkerned advance width (HarfBuzz, `kern` off). About 680 lines per file, pages 11 to 19, 40 to 47 and 105 to 118:

| | median | p10 | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| InDesign | 1.0141 | 1.0082 | 1.0201 |
| DesignCraft | 0.9962 | 0.9907 | 1.0013 |

On the same line in both, "weird and scary noises in the trees ahead of them. Then they start to" at a 293.95 pt measure, the word space is 2.185 pt in InDesign and 2.575 pt in DesignCraft.

Effect: in a 124-page book every story starts on the same page, but inside stories DesignCraft fits more. 80 of 124 pages start at a different character, and a story runs up to 766 characters ahead by its last page.

Reading: #427 fixed the display case in #181, where InDesign's Optical tightens pairs. On body text, InDesign's Optical comes out about 1.4% looser than the font's own advances, while #427's sits about 0.4% tighter. From reading `optical.rs`, the `MAX_LOOSEN = 0.06` em cap and leaving `nn` as set may be what holds it back; we haven't tested that. We can export a reference page from InDesign (OFL font, the same paragraph with Optical and with Metrics) if that would help tune it.

title: PDF export silently drops overset text — `warnings` is empty although preflight reports it
author: stereoscope
body:
**Problem:** `file.exportPdf` writes a PDF without the overset part of a story and returns
`"warnings": []`, while `preflight.run` on the same document reports the frame as an *error*.
In an imported 58-page forms document this removed whole sentences (a data-consent clause, a
statutory break rule, the warning on a sworn declaration) and the last row of two tables, with
no hint anywhere. Text that fits in InDesign overflows in DesignCraft (composition and
hyphenation differ, see #180 and #1428), so imported documents are hit hardest: preflight found
19 overset stories in that document, the export reported none.

**Expectation:** the export result lists overset frames (page, frame id, characters), as
preflight does — or, for CLI/MCP use, an option that fails the export on preflight errors.

**Repro** (`designcraft-cli script 1-overset-export.dcs`):

```
file.new {"width": 300, "height": 200, "pages": 1, "facingPages": false, "margins": 0}
frame.create {"rect": [20, 20, 280, 60], "content": "text", "text": "First line is visible.\nSecond paragraph does not fit: this sentence carries the legal notice and must not vanish from the PDF without a warning."}
story.get {"story": "$1.story"}
preflight.run {}
file.exportPdf {"path": "1-overset-export.pdf"}
```

Result:

- `story.get` → `"overset": 68`
- `preflight.run` → `[{"kind": "overset", "message": "Overset text: 76 characters", "severity": "error", "page": 0}]`
- `file.exportPdf` → `"warnings": []`; the PDF text ends at "…does not fit: this sentence".

Side note: `story.get` and preflight disagree on the count for the same frame (68 vs 76).

**Version:** 0.9.0 · **Platform:** Linux (Fedora 44, x86_64)

The repro files (scripts, IDML, screenshots) follow in a comment.

title: DesignCraft – Essential improvements for professional desktop publishing
author: Thomas47625
body:
# Essential improvements for professional desktop publishing

Hello DesignCraft Development Team,

I have been using Adobe PageMaker professionally for many years to produce funeral stationery, memorial cards, prayer cards and other printed materials requiring precise layouts.

I am currently evaluating DesignCraft as a potential replacement for PageMaker. I appreciate the work behind this project and would very much like to use it for my daily professional production.

However, during my initial tests, I encountered several fundamental issues that currently prevent me from switching to DesignCraft.

I would like to share my observations and suggestions.

## 1. Persistent application preferences – Critical

All user-defined application preferences should be saved permanently and automatically restored when DesignCraft starts or a new document is created.

This should include, among other things:

- Measurement units (millimeters, points, etc.)
- Default stroke widths and colors
- Default fill colors
- Default object properties
- Ruler and guide settings
- Guide colors and snapping behavior
- Ruler origin / zero point
- Grid settings
- Default typography and paragraph settings
- Document defaults and margins
- Workspace and panel arrangements

**Current problem:** Every time I create a new document, the measurement units revert to Picas instead of retaining my preferred millimeters.

Please allow users to define global application defaults while still permitting individual document settings.

A function such as "Save current settings as defaults for new documents" would be very useful.

Related issue: #1400

I created two rectangles, each measuring exactly 50 × 50 mm, and positioned them directly next to each other.

After grouping them, I expected the group to measure exactly 100 × 50 mm.

Instead, DesignCraft displayed:

The deviation was approximately 0.353 mm, equiva…

title: Color Settings: a loaded ICC working space (Edit › Color Settings › Load Profile…) reverts to sRGB / Coated FOGRA39 after a restart
author: ValbyLyntryk
body:
## Summary
After loading an ICC profile with **Edit › Color Settings… › Load Profile…** and choosing it as the RGB or CMYK working space, the choice is saved to `ui.json` by name. On the next start, though, it is reset to the built-in defaults (sRGB IEC61966-2.1 / Coated FOGRA39 (fitted, craft-cms)). Loaded profiles aren't kept or reloaded between sessions, so at startup the saved names count as "unknown" and are replaced. Intent and black point compensation do survive. The result is that a print shop working to a non-built-in condition must reload and reselect its profiles in every session. If someone forgets, PDF/X-4 exports silently get the default output intent.

## Environment
- DesignCraft **0.9.0**, Windows 10 Home 22H2 (build 19045, x64), installer build (`designcraft.exe` / `designcraft-cli.exe`).
- DesignCraft **0.9.0**, Linux x86_64 tarball (Debian 13), `designcraft-cli` (headless).
- Source checked at tags **v0.9.0** and **v0.10.0** and at `main` @ 3ce3a24 (2026-10-21): the relevant code is unchanged.
- Profiles used: `eciRGB_v2.icc` (desc "eciRGB v2") and `eciCMYK_v2.icc` (desc "eciCMYK v2", FOGRA59) from the ECI download. Any non-built-in ICC behaves the same way.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start DesignCraft.
2. **Edit › Color Settings…** › **Load Profile…** › choose `eciRGB_v2.icc`, then **Load Profile…** again › choose `eciCMYK_v2.icc`.
3. Set RGB: **eciRGB v2**, CMYK: **eciCMYK v2**, Intent: Relative Colorimetric, tick *Use Black Point Compensation*, then **OK**.
4. Quit DesignCraft. `ui.json` (`%APPDATA%\DesignCraft\ui.json`, `~/.config/designcraft/ui.json`) now contains
   ```json
   "colorSettings": { "rgb": "eciRGB v2", "cmyk": "eciCMYK v2", "intent": "relativeColorimetric", "bpc": true }
   ```
5. Start DesignCraft again and open **Edit › Color Settings…** (or export a PDF/X-4).

Headless equivalent: every new engine session starts with only the built-in profiles, so applying the saved names before loading fails:
```
$ designcraft-cli run --samp…

title: PDF/X output intent: let the OutputConditionIdentifier be set (e.g. FOGRA59) instead of always "Custom" for loaded ICC profiles
author: ValbyLyntryk
body:
With a loaded CMYK working space, PDF/X-4 export embeds the right ICC as `DestOutputProfile` but always writes `/OutputConditionIdentifier (Custom)` (with `/OutputCondition` = the profile description). Only the built-in Coated FOGRA39 gets a registered identifier (`FOGRA39`). Source: `Cms::output_intent()` in [`crates/color/src/cms/mod.rs` L333–L343](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/blob/v0.9.0/crates/color/src/cms/mod.rs#L333-L343), used by `crates/pdf/src/pdfx.rs` L49; unchanged in v0.10.0 and on `main`.

Example (0.9.0, eciCMYK v2 loaded as the CMYK working space; `validate-pdf` reports the file valid):
```
/S /GTS_PDFX /OutputConditionIdentifier (Custom) /OutputCondition (eciCMYK v2) /Info (eciCMYK v2) /RegistryName (http://www.color.org)
```
Preflight tools and print providers often match on the registered identifier (here `FOGRA59`, the ICC/Fogra characterisation for eciCMYK v2).

**Request:** a field in Color Settings or the Export PDF dialog (and a `file.exportPdf` / `color.settings` parameter) for the output condition identifier, condition and registry name. Alternatively, a lookup of well-known profiles (FOGRA39/51/52/59, CGATS21 CRPC 1–7, GRACoL…) by profile description or ID, falling back to "Custom" only when unknown.

Related: #1474

title: Color Settings: colour management policies (e.g. CMYK "Preserve Numbers"), as in other DTP apps
author: ValbyLyntryk
body:
Edit › Color Settings in 0.9.0 has RGB/CMYK working spaces, intent and BPC, but no colour management policies: what happens to placed or imported CMYK content whose profile differs from, or is missing against, the CMYK working space. Print workflows usually want **Preserve Numbers (ignore linked profiles)** for CMYK, so that CMYK values in placed PDFs/images and swatches reach the output unchanged. They also want an explicit choice (Preserve embedded / Convert to working space / Off) for RGB, plus optional mismatch warnings. It would be good to have these policies (and matching `color.settings` parameters), with Preserve Numbers documented as the CMYK default if that is already the effective behaviour. #684 (document colour profiles) is related.

Related: #1474

title: PDF export: write overprint (honour "Overprint [Black] Swatch at 100%" and the Attributes overprint settings)
author: ValbyLyntryk
body:
In 0.9.0 the document setting *Overprint [Black] Swatch at 100%* (on by default, `overprint_black`) only affects Overprint Preview (`crates/render/src/lib.rs` L1097–L1100). PDF export writes no overprint (`/OP`, `/op`, `/OPM` ExtGState): `crates/pdf/src/lib.rs` L28 lists overprint under "Not yet". Object or text overprint settings only produce the warning "overprint is not exported yet" (`crates/pdf/src/export.rs` L957–L958, `crates/pdf/src/text.rs` L486–L487). So small 100 % K text on a tinted background knocks out in print, which risks white halos from misregistration on offset presses.

**Request:** export overprint in PDF/X-4 (ExtGState `/OP true /op true /OPM 1` for overprinting fills/strokes/text, and automatically for [Black] at 100 % when that setting is on).

Related: #1474

title: Feature Request: Better Equation Editing
author: yamisama
body:
Instead of modelling the math feature after InDesign, it would be better to fully integrate the equation editor with the typesetting engine and offer the user real WYSIWYG editing similar to equation editors like MathType and full typographical control over equations, such as kerning, fonts, baseline shifting, character styles and formatting of all individual elements, as well as integration of inline graphics.

InDesign's equation feature was tucked on by Adobe with the bare minimum effort and doesn't even separate into CMYK plates correctly since it is based on a JavaScript library only intended for web usage. We should not be emulating it.

LaTeX editing/roundtripping should also be retained and expanded on (better UI, syntax higlighting etc.) since it is a common way of typing equations that many users from the scientific community are familiar with. It also facilitates exchange of equations with other software and makes it possible to display equations inline in the Story Editor. Consequently, the feature should be designed from the start in a way that makes it easy to move back and forth between LaTeX and WYSIWYG representation.

title: Pasting text from another app into a text frame anchors previously copied objects instead
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### Description

When you edit a text frame and paste text copied in another app (e.g. a text editor), nothing visible appears. DesignCraft inserts an anchored object instead of the text, if objects (a graphic frame, shape, line…) were copied earlier in the same session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Copy any non-text object in DesignCraft (e.g. an empty graphic frame).
2. In another app, copy some text, e.g. `17 Stand 223`.
3. Back in DesignCraft, click into a text frame and press Ctrl+V.

**Expected:** `17 Stand 223` is inserted at the insertion point.
**Actual:** the previously copied object is anchored into the text. It shows up only as an invisible character, and the clipboard text is lost.

Ctrl+Shift+V (paste without formatting) is not affected.

Engine-only reproduction with the CLI:

```sh
# with an earlier object copy → the clipboard text is ignored
designcraft-cli run --cmd file.new \
  --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[72,400,200,500],"content":"graphic"}' --cmd edit.copy \
  --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[72,72,400,300],"content":"text","text":"Hello"}' \
  --cmd 'text.select={"story":10,"anchor":5,"focus":5}' \
  --cmd 'edit.paste={"text":"17 Stand 223"}'
# → {"anchored":1,"pos":8}

# without it → the text is pasted
designcraft-cli run --cmd file.new \
  --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[72,72,400,300],"content":"text","text":"Hello"}' \
  --cmd 'text.select={"story":9,"anchor":5,"focus":5}' \
  --cmd 'edit.paste={"text":"17 Stand 223"}'
# → {"pos":17}
```

### Cause

`paste_text` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` anchors the copied items whenever no text was copied in DesignCraft since. It does not check whether `text`, the system clipboard's text, is present:

```rust
if formatted
    && clip.is_none()
    && t.cell.is_none()
    && let Some(items) = s.clipboard.clone()
```

The UI already removes `text` when the clipboard still holds the placeholder of DesignCraft's own object copy (`with_system_clipboard` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`). So a `text` that reache…

title: Drop shadow: Effects panel reads Distance and Size in points, the Effects dialog in document units; dialog colour menu has no colour chips
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### Description

The drop shadow can be set in two places, the quick settings in the Effects panel and the Effects dialog (the **fx** button). They edit the same shadow but read numbers differently. And the dialog's colour menu doesn't show the colour of the swatch.

**1. Panel and dialog use different units.** The panel always shows and reads Distance and Size in points (`7 pt`, `5 pt`). The dialog uses the document's ruler units. In a document set to picas (the default for Letter), the dialog shows `0p7` and `0p5`, and a bare number typed there is read in picas:

1. New document (Letter, picas), draw a frame with a fill, turn on Drop Shadow in the Effects panel.
2. Open the Effects dialog with **fx** and type `7` as Distance and `5` as Size, then OK.
3. The panel now shows `84 pt` and `60 pt`.

With a 60 pt blur, the shadow is a faint, wide haze around the object. On a coloured background, that doesn't look like a shadow at all. Typed into the panel, the same numbers give a normal shadow. So the two places seem to work against each other.

**2. The dialog's colour menu only lists names.** The Color menu on the Drop Shadow page (and the other effect pages) is a plain list of swatch names, with no colour chip for the current swatch or in the list. Other swatch menus show chips. You can't see what colour the shadow has without knowing the swatch.

### Expected

- Distance and Size in the panel use the document's units, as the dialog does, so a typed `7` means the same in both.
- The dialog's colour menu shows the chosen swatch's colour and a chip per swatch.

### Related, not part of this

The Drop Shadow page also lacks some common options: a blend mode for the shadow (it is always mixed Normal, so on a coloured background it greys the colour instead of darkening it), Noise, and "Object Knocks Out Shadow". Those need renderer work and are worth their own issue.

### Environment

Linux (KDE Plasma, Wayland session, app via XWayland), current `main`.

title: Editing freezes for half a second or more per step with large placed images in a CMYK blend space
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What happens

With a few large placed images and transparency in the spread, every edit makes the canvas freeze. Moving or drawing an object, or nudging it with the arrow keys, takes about half a second per step in a 1400 × 900 window, and several seconds in a large window or zoomed in. Aligning objects by hand is almost impossible.

The CPU is not the limit; it's the time each new frame takes.

### Steps

1. A document in a CMYK blend space (the default for print) with a 3840 × 5760 PSD with transparency and two 1254 × 1254 PNGs placed on one spread.
2. Draw a frame or move an object over them, at any zoom.

### Measured

Each step re-renders the changed area in about 450 ms (300–400 ms of it converting images to their ink plates), the same at 50 % and at 800 %.

title: Gradient Swatch tool sets the frame's gradient instead of the selected text's
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What happens

A gradient can be applied to text or to part of a text (the text's fill set to a gradient swatch). But when the Gradient Swatch tool (G) is then dragged across that text, the drag sets the gradient on the **frame's fill**, not on the text. The text gradient can't be positioned at all.

### Steps

1. Draw a text frame, type a word and select it with the Type tool.
2. Apply a gradient swatch to the selected text.
3. Choose the Gradient Swatch tool and drag across the text.

### Expected

With text selected (or a text frame selected with Formatting Affects Text on), the drag sets where the text's gradient starts and ends, for the selected characters only.

### Why

The tool always sends `object.gradient {ids, from, to}`, which edits an object's fill or stroke. Text has no gradient start and end of its own: a gradient on text is always laid across the whole frame's box (`text_area` in `crates/render/src/text.rs`). Supporting this needs a gradient vector in the character attributes (start, length and angle per character), its use when text is drawn and exported, its IDML round trip (`GradientFillStart`, `GradientFillLength`, `GradientFillAngle` on character ranges), and the tool sending it as a character attribute when text is the target.

title: Line Numbers, as InDesign's (every Nth line, with position and counting options)
author: EgalNormal
body:
InDesign offers Layout → Line Numbers (paragraph style option), with:

- enable per paragraph style, with an option to count every Nth line (e.g. 5 → shows 5, 10, 15 …) or every line
- position: left/right of the text frame, with a distance and alignment
- count mode: per line vs. per paragraph; restart options
- optional: skip empty lines / suppress for specific paragraphs (in Word that's "Suppress Line Numbers")

Continuing numbering across text frames: When a document has several text frames (e.g. one source text per frame on a history exam), the numbers should continue across frames by default, not restart per frame. Ideally there is also a way to set an explicit start number for a frame or paragraph (similar to InDesign's "Start at" for page/section numbering or Word's "Set Numbering Value") — e.g. source A runs 1–48, then source B in a second frame continues at 49.

Use case: proofreading manuscripts, and exam papers with source texts that need line numbers for reference (e.g. history/language exams). A per-paragraph-style toggle with an interval and frame-spanning continuation is the minimum to make this useful.

title: Changing the interface language at runtime breaks menu commands, keyboard shortcuts and dropdowns
author: stefanobaraldo1-creator
body:
Changing the interface language at runtime breaks menu commands, keyboard shortcuts and dropdowns

Environment: DesignCraft 0.10.0, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M4 Pro (Metal), installed via ArtCraft Launcher.

Steps to reproduce

Launch DesignCraft (English).
Open Settings (Cmd+K) → General → Interface Language → select any other language (tested: Italiano, Deutsch) → OK.
The UI is correctly translated, but now try any menu bar command (e.g. DesignCraft → Settings…, View → Show/Hide Rulers) or shortcut (Cmd+K, Cmd+R).

Expected: menu commands and shortcuts keep working.

Actual:

No menu bar command or keyboard shortcut has any effect.
ComboBox dropdowns inside windows no longer open, e.g. the language selector when Settings is reopened via the in-app search.
Plain buttons and in-window clicks still work, e.g. New file → Create.
Quit (Cmd+Q / menu) also does nothing, so the app must be force-quit, and the new language is never saved.

Notes

This is not a hang. A sample of the process taken in this state shows the main thread idle in the normal event loop (NSApplication run → mach_msg), with no busy threads. The log shows no errors or panics.
The translations themselves are fine. With "language": "it" set manually in ui.json before launch, the app starts in Italian and menus and shortcuts work normally.
Switching at runtime breaks it in every direction tested, including Italian → English. So the bug seems to be in the runtime language switch, probably the native menu or command bindings being rebuilt with the new locale, not in a specific translation.

**Version:** DesignCraft 0.10.0 (desktop app + designcraft-cli), Windows 10 Pro. Document last saved with 0.6.0.

## What happens

After updating to 0.10.0, an unchanged 32-page document opens with its text in different positions. Frame geometry is identical (every frame, fill, stroke and image is where it was), but text inside the frames has moved, and some text has disappeared into overset.

The cause seems to be a different ascent value for the font. Since 0.10.0 the ascent comes from a different table in the font file:

| Font table value (Trebuchet MS, 2048 units/em) | Ratio | First baseline at 24 pt |
|---|---|---|
| `hhea.ascent` = `OS/2.usWinAscent` = 1923 | 0.939 | 22.54 pt (0.6.0) |
| `OS/2.sTypoAscender` = 1510 | 0.737 | 17.70 pt (0.10.0) |

Measured in exported PDFs, the 0.6.0 and 0.10.0 results match these two values exactly.

1. In 0.6.0: new document, text frame at y = 60 pt, inset 0, vertical justification Top, First Baseline Offset **Ascent**.
2. Type a line in Trebuchet MS Bold 24 pt / 27 pt leading. Save, export PDF.
3. Open the same file in 0.10.0 and export a PDF again.

**Expected:** first baseline at 82.54 pt (60 + 22.54), as in 0.6.0.
**Actual:** first baseline at 77.70 pt (60 + 17.70). The text moves up by 4.84 pt.

title: [audit DC-01] PDF export post-passes can be misled by document content (High)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Category:** output integrity · **Confidence:** Plausible (traced by reading, not executed)

**Affected:** the PDF export post-processing passes in `crates/pdf/src/transitions.rs` (`object()` and the passes that use it: `add_blend_space`, `add_catalog_entries`, `add_page_entries`, `add_transitions`), `crates/pdf/src/pdfx.rs`, and media embedding in `crates/pdf/src/forms.rs`, driven from `crates/engine/src/cmd/export.rs`.

**Summary:** after the main PDF is written, the post-passes find existing objects (catalog, page tree, pages) by text search over the output bytes, taking the last match. Document-controlled bytes written into the PDF earlier in the pipeline can therefore be mistaken for those objects, so a crafted document can alter the structure of the PDFs a user exports from it. The media MIME type is also written into a PDF name with only `/` escaped.

**Impact:** the integrity of exported PDFs that users go on to distribute.

**Suggested fix direction:**
- Don't rediscover objects by text search. Carry the object offsets each pass writes, or resolve objects through the xref chain and check that `N 0 obj` starts exactly at the recorded offset.
- Escape every PDF-name byte outside the regular-character set as `#xx`.
- Replace the two-`find` slices with `get()` (see the related robustness issue for the post-pass slice panics).

Reproduction details and a test are available to maintainers privately.

---

title: [audit DC-03] Per-reference deep copies in XLSX and DOCX import (High)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Category:** DoS (amplification) · **Confidence:** Confirmed

**Location:** `textimport/src/xlsx.rs:53`; `textimport/src/docx.rs:407-418`

**Evidence.**
- `textimport/src/xlsx.rs:53`: `Some("s") => v().trim().parse::<usize>().ok().and_then(|i| shared.get(i).cloned())`. Every cell is collected (`:112`, `:222`) **before** `MAX_CELLS = 100_000` is applied to the grid (`:233`).
- `textimport/src/docx.rs:407-411`:
  ```rust
  "footnoteReference" if allow_notes => {
      if let Some(note) = e.attr("id").and_then(|id| self.footnotes.get(id).cloned()) {
          let mut ns = Story::new(StoryId(0));
          self.blocks(&note, &mut ns, false);
  ```

**Scenario.**
- **XLSX:** one ~1–60 MB `<si>` shared string and ~3M `<c t="s"><v>0</v></c>` cells means TB-scale allocation and an abort, both on File › Place and as a data merge source.
- **DOCX:** one ~1 MB footnote referenced ~100k times (~3.5 MB of XML) means ~100 GB of note stories. `insert_note` is also O(n) per call.

**Fix sketch.**
```diff
-        Some("s") => v().trim().parse::<usize>().ok().and_then(|i| shared.get(i).cloned()).unwrap_or_default(),
+        // store the index; materialize text only for cells inside the kept range,
+        // and keep a running byte budget (e.g. 64 MiB) across all cells
+        Some("s") => Cell::Shared(v().trim().parse::<usize>().ok()?),
```
For DOCX, import each footnote id once. Later references to the same id get an empty note and a warning. Cap total note text.

title: [audit DC-04] Control channel (--control) has no authentication (Medium)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Category:** authentication / local privilege boundary · **Confidence:** Confirmed

**Affected:** `apps/designcraft/src/control_server.rs` and the request dispatch in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`.

**Summary:** when the app is started with `--control <port>` or `DESIGNCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`, the loopback control channel runs requests without any authentication. It reaches every engine command, including file open, save and export with arbitrary paths, and quitting without saving. The `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` confinement exists only for the in-process `designcraft-cli mcp`, so it doesn't apply to this channel. The existing hardening is good: opt-in, loopback only, non-JSON first lines rejected (so browser requests can't run commands), and line-length and connection limits.

**Impact:** on multi-user machines, or with other local software that can reach loopback, a process that isn't the user can act with the user's file permissions while the channel is on.

**Suggested fix direction:**
- Require a per-launch random token (written 0600 to the profile directory and/or printed for the launcher) as the first line of each connection.
- Optionally let the GUI accept automation roots so control-driven commands can be confined.

Further details are available to maintainers privately.

title: [audit DC-06] DOM and JSON memory expansion without node-count caps (Medium)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Category:** DoS (memory expansion) · **Confidence:** Plausible

**Location:** `idml/src/xml.rs:204-276`; `idml/src/import.rs:97-99,143-147`; `format/src/lib.rs:208,293`; `textimport/src/docx.rs:66-140`

**Evidence.**
- `idml/src/xml.rs:204-276` bounds nesting depth (`MAX_DEPTH = 256`) only. Per-part (512 MiB) and total (2 GiB) byte budgets are applied to decompressed bytes (`idml/src/import.rs:143-147`).
- Each `<a/>` (4 bytes) becomes a `Node` of ~72–80 bytes plus a heap-allocated name. `import.rs:97-99` clones elements (`top.extend(el.elements().cloned())`, `c.clone()`).
- DOCX builds the same kind of `El` tree (`textimport/src/docx.rs:66-140`) for parts of up to 64 MiB each.
- The native format parses up to 256 MiB of `document.json` into a `serde_json::Value` (`format/src/lib.rs:208`). The legacy path clones it (`:293`).

**Scenario.** A 512 MiB part of `<a/>` deflates to about 0.5 MB, and up to four fit the budget. That's 15–25 GB per part, which is an OOM abort.

**Fix sketch.** Add an element-count budget to `parse` (e.g. ≤ 10M nodes per import, shared across parts) and move elements instead of cloning them. For the native format, deserialize `Document` straight from the byte slice (`serde_json::from_slice::<Document>`) instead of going through `Value`.

title: [audit DC-08] Non-finite IDML numbers corrupt the saved document (Medium)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Category:** Data integrity · **Confidence:** Plausible

**Location:** `idml/src/import.rs:390` (`nums`) → 438, 465, 614, 890-895, 2495; `format/src/lib.rs:72`

**Evidence.**
- `idml/src/import.rs:390`: `fn nums(s: &str) -> Vec<f64> { s.split_whitespace().filter_map(|v| v.parse().ok()).collect() }`. Note that `"NaN"` and `"inf"` parse as `f64`. A `finite_nums` exists (`:395`) but isn't used everywhere.
- `nums` feeds:
  - `parse_affine` (`:438`) and `parse_point` (`:465`)
  - `PasteboardMargins` (`:614`)
  - `color_of` (`:890-895`), where values like `1e300` also become `inf` after `as f32`
  - page `GeometricBounds` (`:2495`)
- `format/src/lib.rs:70-72` refuses to save only when an *item* is non-finite (`doc.non_finite_item()`).

**Scenario.**
- **NaN item transform:** the user can't save their work at all, and the recovery autosave fails the same way.
- **NaN page bounds, swatch or setting:** serde_json writes `null`, and the next open fails with "invalid type: null, expected f64". The saved file is silently unreadable.

**Fix sketch.**
```diff
-fn nums(s: &str) -> Vec<f64> { s.split_whitespace().filter_map(|v| v.parse().ok()).collect() }
+fn nums(s: &str) -> Vec<f64> { s.split_whitespace().filter_map(|v| v.parse::<f64>().ok()).filter(|v| v.is_finite()).collect() }
```
Also extend the pre-save check to pages, swatches and settings (a whole-document `non_finite()` walk), and check composed transforms after `parent * xf`.

title: [audit DC-09] Deep nesting vs. the Windows 1 MB main-thread stack (Medium)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Category:** DoS (stack overflow) · **Confidence:** Needs verification

**Location:** `idml/src/import.rs:2984,3014,2289-2449`; usvg depth 1024

**Evidence.**
- XML depth is capped at 256 (`idml/src/xml.rs:201`), but the importer recurses once per level with large frames:
  - nested `Group` → `item()` (`import.rs:2984,3014`)
  - `walk_story` (`:2289-2449`)
  - table → `story_with_para` → `walk_story` (`:2216,2334`)
- `file.open` runs synchronously on the UI thread, and the repo sets no `stack_size`.
- usvg allows XML depth 1,024, and its converter and resvg recurse per level. `natural_size` parses SVGs at place time on the UI thread.

**Impact.** Stack overflow is an uncatchable abort.

**Verification test.** Import an IDML with 250 nested `<Group>`s and render an SVG with 1,000 nested `<g opacity=".5">`, each on `std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(1 << 20)`, in both debug and release builds.

**Fix.** Lower the page-item and range nesting budget (e.g. 64, as `Document::check` uses for anchored frames), or run import and SVG parsing on a worker thread with an explicit 16–64 MB stack.

body:

-let kids_str = &kids_str[kids_str.find('[')? + 1..kids_str.find(']')?];
+let open = kids_str.find('[')?; let close = kids_str[open..].find(']')? + open;

```

title: [Feature Request] Please add official OpenCode skill support for DesignCraft
author: AHL8192
body:
Thanks for DesignCraft — threaded stories and styles are exactly the kind of thing agents get wrong without a map.

DesignCraft is one of those rare apps where the agent surface is a first-class citizen rather than a bolted-on API: 521 headless commands in 64 namespaces, 685 app commands, 26 MCP tools, and a control channel that speaks the same engine as the GUI. That is 90% of the work, and it is why this request is small.

## Why a skill, when the MCP server already exists?

An MCP server answers *"what can this app do?"*. A skill answers *"what should an agent do next, in what order, with which ids, and which footguns should it avoid?"*

The gap we kept falling into:

| Without a skill | With a skill |
|---|---|
| Command ids discovered by trial and error | Namespaces and ids named up front |
| Coordinates and units guessed | Conventions stated once, with the failure mode |
| Silent coercions quietly corrupt output | Known coercions listed, with the read-back that catches them |
| Every session re-derives the workflow | Verified recipes to copy |

MCP makes DesignCraft *possible* to drive. A skill makes it *reliable* to drive — in the same way your own docs do for a human.

## The ask

- [ ] **Ship the skill in-tree** — e.g. `.opencode/skills/designcraft/SKILL.md` alongside `references/` and `scripts/`, versioned with the app
- [ ] **One line in the README** next to the MCP section saying how to install it
- [ ] **Regenerate the volatile bits at release** (version, tool count, command ids) — the included scripts do most of this already

## What we're handing over

title: Drop shadow / outer glow Spread grows the frame of a transparent image, not what it paints
author: PiMinusMax
body:
**What happens:** A drop shadow or outer glow with Spread on a placed image with transparency (a PNG cut-out, a logo) grows the *frame's* outline, not what the image paints. The transparent part of the frame casts a hard dark band along the frame edge, as wide as the spread part of Size. Without Spread the shadow follows the image's pixels, as expected.

**Steps:**
1. Place a PNG with a transparent background in a frame larger than its visible content.
2. Object › Effects › Drop Shadow: Size 1.5 cm, Spread 50%.
3. A dark rounded rectangle appears around the whole frame, though only the cut-out should cast a shadow.

**Why:** `fx.rs` grows the silhouette by stroking the frame's path (`grow * 2` wide) whenever the object "paints its area" (a fill, an image or pasted-in items). For an image with transparent pixels the path is not what it paints.

**Expected:** Spread hardens and widens the shadow of what is painted: the image's opaque pixels, a text frame's glyphs, a filled shape's area.

title: Drop shadow and outer glow on a group are not drawn
author: PiMinusMax
body:
**What happens:** Drop Shadow and Outer Glow set on a group are stored (the Effects panel and dialog show them, `object.dropShadow` with the group's id succeeds) but never drawn. The group's objects show no shadow at all.

**Steps:**
1. Draw two rectangles, select both, Object › Group.
2. Object › Effects › Drop Shadow, OK.
3. Nothing changes on the canvas or in the export. Ungroup and apply the shadow to each rectangle and it shows.

**Why:** `Renderer::draw_item_inner` draws a group by drawing its children (plus Gradient Feather, opacity and blending); the `draw_item_fx` path with the below-object effects is only taken for leaf objects.

**Expected:** The group's objects cast one shadow (or glow) together, under all of them, as for a single object.
